Using an intersection-over-union objective and evaluation metric (range-IoU), RangeFinder achieves a range-IoU of $0.464 \pm 0.002$, outperforming all deployable baselines while requiring only $12.2$ ms per pocket. We also quantify our method's ability to reduce the ligand search space while retaining compatible binders; in this regard, RangeFinder achieves a Reduction-Recall F-Score of $0.543 \pm 0.011$ --- once again outperforming all deployable baselines. Ablation experiments indicate that RangeFinder's performance depends more strongly on the density and quality of ligand supervision than on any individual input modality or specialized training strategy. Together, these results position RangeFinder as an inexpensive and effective molecular filtering prior, with demonstrated potential in narrowing the ligand search space of target pockets before docking, generation, or synthesis. The code for this project can be found at: https://github.com/alannadels/RangeFinder.

title: Piezogyration and elastogyration in ternary chalcopyrites from first principles
abstract: Natural optical activity arises from the spatial dispersion of the optical response and is described by the rank-two gyration pseudotensor. Its dependence on mechanical stress and strain, quantified by the piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, respectively, has been investigated experimentally for decades. However, a systematic first-principles description of these effects remains largely unexplored. Here we present a first-principles methodology to compute the full piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, and apply it to a set of representative ternary chalcopyrite crystals. The gyration of the unstrained crystal turns out to be a poor predictor of the magnitude of the elastogyration response, which we find to be a property inherited from their parent zinc-blende structures. The elastic compliance tensor further shapes the piezogyration response, with particularly pronounced effects in AgGaS$_2$, a well-known achiral yet optically active crystal. Finally, we explore strain-induced chirality through the trace of the gyration tensor, the only pseudoscalar contribution to the natural optical activity that is linear in the tensor components and encodes information about chirality.

title: Guest-Programmed Adaptive Redistribution in Heteroleptic Metal–Organic Cages
abstract: Adaptive reconfiguration of complex supramolecular assemblies remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry, especially for heteroleptic systems prone to kinetic traps and component scrambling. Here, we report a guest-coupled reassembly strategy that enables programmable redistribution between cage architectures in heteroleptic pentagonal prismatic ZnII cages, assembled via precise edge-length matching between pentatopic and tetratopic ligands. Distinct from conventional single-guest templation, these cages exhibit adaptive redistribution behavior in which multiguest recognition is coupled to host redistribution within confined cavities. Chlorinated guests are selectively encapsulated through Cl···π and π···π interactions, thereby biasing the thermodynamic landscape of assembly. Secondary guests redirect the assembly equilibrium toward distinct product distributions, including guest release, guest exchange, or stoichiometry-dependent formation of species assigned as a homoleptic pseudo-cubic cage with one or two encapsulated guests. Crystallographic, Hirshfeld surface, and computational analyses reveal that multiple Cl···π, π···π, and C–H···π noncovalent interactions within the confined cavity contribute to the selectivity of guest-directed assembly redistribution. Furthermore, the incorporation of peripheral pyrene units imparts the prismatic cages with photoluminescence, which is enhanced upon guest binding due to framework rigidification. This work demonstrates how confined multiguest recognition can be coupled to compositional redistribution within complex heteroleptic assemblies, providing a foundation for programmable adaptive supramolecular systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Target Specific Conformational Flexibility and Electrostatic Complementarity Modulate LTNF10 Peptide Binding to Phospholipase A2 Variants from Snake Venoms
abstract: Phospholipase A2 is one of the primary cytotoxins present in snake venoms, causing tissue damage through the hydrolysis of phospholipids in the cellular membrane. We prioritised and investigated in detail the binding and conformational dynamics of a ten-residue short peptide (LTNF10) from Lethal Toxin Neutralizing Factor from Opossum against snake venom Phospholipase A2 (svPLA2) variants. LTNF10 was prioritised from the curated list of peptide inhibitors.

title: Stereodivergent Synthesis of γ-Functionalized Primary Alcohols via Relay-Synergistic Ir/Amine/Ni Catalysis
abstract: Primary alcohols bearing chiral motifs constitute a class of highly valuable organic compounds that are widely prevalent in natural products and pharmaceutical molecules. Although impressive progress has been made in α- and β-functionalization of primary alcohols, the development of efficient methods for the synthesis of the γ-functionalized primary alcohols─particularly in an asymmetric fashion─remains a significant challenge.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Interfacial Anion Activation for Durable Aqueous Zn-Ion Batteries
abstract: Designing a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is pivotal for stabilizing the Zn anode/electrolyte interface in aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, the mechanism of SEI formation in AZIBs remains insufficiently understood, particularly when additives induce the formation of mixed inorganic and organic SEI components during electrochemical reactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Engagement-Supportive Mechanisms in Stress-Focused Digital Mental Health Interventions With Adaptive, Conversational, and Context-Aware Systems: Narrative Review
abstract: BackgroundStress is a widespread public health concern associated with cardiovascular disease, depression, anxiety, and reduced quality of life. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs), delivered through smartphones, web platforms, and wearables, offer scalable support for stress management but often struggle to sustain user engagement. Evidence describing how adaptive, conversational, and context-aware mechanisms function together within stress-focused DMHIs remains fragmented.ObjectiveThis review aims to synthesize evidence on engagement-supportive mechanisms in stress-focused DMHIs, with attention to personalization; biometric feedback; just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs); gamification; AI, including large language models (LLMs); and methodological approaches to studying engagement. It also examines methodological, motivational, and experiential dimensions of engagement.MethodsThis narrative review was informed by a structured search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2018 and April 2025, followed by an evidence update through August 2026. Eligible studies described stress-focused DMHIs or related affective support interventions reporting at least 1 engagement-supportive mechanism. Randomized controlled trials, qualitative investigations, simulation or modeling studies, and implementation studies were included. Data were extracted using a structured form capturing study characteristics, engagement mechanisms, outcomes, and alignment with the review domains. Descriptive mapping summarized study types and mechanism frequencies, while a narrative synthesis integrated behavioral, experiential, methodological, and theory-informed findings.ResultsThirty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. Randomized or microrandomized controlled trials were the most common design (n=17), followed by qualitative investigations (n=6), design or implementation studies (n=3), mixed methods studies (n=3), simulation or modeling studies (n=2), and a quasi-experimental study (n=1). Dynamic adaptation was identified in 14 studies, conversational support in 10, static tailoring in 9, social or co-design mechanisms in 9, context-aware prompting in 7, gamified reinforcement in 5, biometric-responsive adaptation in 4, and narrative immersion in 2. These mechanisms frequently overlapped within layered adaptive architectures rather than functioning as isolated engagement features. AI-enabled systems included conversational agents, LLM-supported systems, recommender systems, reinforcement learning, and computational modeling approaches. Outcomes included behavioral indicators such as adherence, retention, and prompt receptivity, alongside experiential indicators such as perceived relevance, trust, emotional support, and immersion. Evidence strength varied substantially; many AI-enabled systems contributed feasibility, acceptability, or optimization-oriented evidence rather than definitive comparative effectiveness evidence.ConclusionsStress-focused DMHIs are increasingly adopting adaptive, conversational, and context-aware engagement-supportive mechanisms, but the evidence base remains heterogeneous and methodologically uneven. Dynamic adaptation, conversational support, and static tailoring were most frequently represented, whereas biometric-responsive adaptation, narrative immersion, and deeply integrated gamified systems were less common. AI-enabled systems may support contextual responsiveness and personalized interaction but require transparent adaptive logic, privacy safeguards, and human-centered evaluation. Future work should prioritize longitudinal, mixed methods research capable of distinguishing behavioral engagement, experiential engagement, feasibility, acceptability, and sustained stress-related outcomes.

title: Joule Heating Induced Structural Evolution of Ordered Mesoporous Mg-Al Spinel-Related Oxides
abstract: Coupling block copolymer self-assembly with ultrafast Joule heating enables second-scale crystallization of ordered mesoporous oxides while preserving long-range mesoscopic order. Using this strategy, we synthesize long-range ordered mesoporous magnesium-aluminum oxide frameworks at low magnesium contents exhibiting defect spinel-related nanocrystalline structures. Ex situ isothermal holds at 1000 to 1155 °C reveal rapid crystallite enlargement followed by a plateau in apparent crystallite size.

title: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction
abstract: Protein-complex structure prediction with AlphaFold 3 depends on MSA content, depth, and cross-chain pairing. Current pipelines apply uniform recipes, typically maximizing depth and pairing by species, yet even whether cross-chain pairing helps AF3 remains contested. We show that the value of both depth and pairing is strongly target-dependent, so no single recipe is optimal across interfaces. We introduce an autonomous agent that treats a frozen AF3 as a black-box experimental instrument. For each target, the agent formulates biological hypotheses, analyzes and reorganizes the MSA, and iteratively refines sequence selection and pairing using predictor label-free signals alone. On 1{,}015 protein--protein interfaces from three benchmarks released after AF3's training cutoff, the agent improves overall interface DockQ over AF3's default pipeline and fixed MSA recipes on every benchmark, while using on average 60\% fewer MSA sequences than the default. Gains are largest for inter-species heteromers, where species-based pairing is unreliable: mean DockQ increases from 0.465 to 0.612 on FoldBench and from 0.482 to 0.562 on HD439. The improvements arise from both sequence construction and pairing policy, including deliberate non-pairing. These results recast MSA design as a target-specific problem and show that an autonomous agent can adapt it at test time through biological reasoning and self-directed, confidence-guided experimentation.

title: Pressure-correlation phase diagram unraveling quantum phase transitions in altermagnetic $ε$-FeOOH and realization of piezo-anomalous Hall effect
abstract: We establish a pressure-correlation phase diagram that yields multiple pressure-tunable quantum phase transitions in iron oxyhydroxide ($ε$-FeOOH) across three critical pressures, $P_{c1}>P_{c2}>P_{c3}$. The transitions arise from the competition among electron-correlation, crystal-field, and Hund's coupling. First-principles calculations reveal that the earlier reported high-spin (HS) to low-spin (LS) crossover at correlation-sensitive $P_{c1}$ is accompanied by a transition from charge-transfer to Mott insulating (CTI-MI) phase, and a change in the spin-quantization axis (SQA) from $\hat{y}$ to $\hat{x}$. The HS-LS crossover and CTI-MI transition is driven by the simultaneous increase in crystal-field splitting and decrease in Hund's coupling. The critical pressure $P_{c2}$ governing the structural transition from centrosymmetric $Pnnm$ phase to noncentrosymmetric $P2_1nm$ phase is found to be independent of electron-correlation. When correlation is strong, a third critical pressure ($P_{c3}$) emerges in the lower-pressure regime of the phase diagram. Validating the recent experimental observation, $P_{c3}$ is responsible for changing the SQA from $\hat{z}$ to $\hat{y}$. By exhibiting altermagnetism in both $P2_1nm$ and $Pnnm$ phases and possessing finite anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) only for SQA along $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$, $ε$-FeOOH enables a unique piezo-anomalous Hall effect where one can switch on the AHC at a lower pressure and change its direction at a higher pressure.

title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
abstract: A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.

title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
abstract: LaBraM, an early EEG foundation model, demonstrated that large-scale EEG pretraining can yield strong representations for diverse downstream tasks. Building on this foundation, we expand pretraining data and model capacity while retaining its core encoder and objective. We train ten encoders with 5.8 million to 1.97 billion parameters on three EEG collections spanning 25,067 to 79,910 hours, adapting signal preparation and training to heterogeneous recordings. Across 23 tasks, Atom-L* reaches 59.05% mean balanced accuracy at its best evaluated full fine-tuning (Full-FT) checkpoint, 3.61 percentage points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model. Quark-G leads linear probing (LP) at 54.33%, a 1.24-point margin. Both also lead average task rank. At the last evaluated checkpoints, larger encoders improve Full-FT more consistently than LP, and stronger LP does not guarantee stronger Full-FT. Preserving patch structure improves LP over average pooling. Data-fraction experiments suggest capacity-dependent saturation, while checkpoint trajectories show that downstream performance can decline as pretraining loss falls. Joint classification with a shared Qwen3 readout reaches 50.50% with Molecule-H and Qwen3-8B; increasing language-model size provides no consistent gain. These results demonstrate the value of scaling LaBraM and the importance of matching pretraining scale to downstream adaptation.

title: Ultrafast Polar Topology Reversal via THz-Driven Inertial Switching
abstract: Topological polar structures in ferroelectric heterostructures offer functional states beyond ordinary domains. As polarization reversal underpins ferroelectric devices, switching between degenerate topological variants, which we refer to as topology reversal, would greatly expand the ways to control polar textures. However, polar topology reversal is challenging because it requires coordinated flipping of oppositely oriented local polarizations, a process not naturally driven by a uniform electric field. Using a multiscale modeling approach, we show that polar topology can be stabilized and reversed in a simple Pt/PbTiO$_3$/Pt nanocapacitor. Electrode-controlled boundary conditions drive tetragonal PbTiO$_3$ into competing orthorhombic- and rhombohedral-like polarization states, which form building blocks for diverse topological structures, including vortex arrays, skyrmion lattices, dipole spirals, and dipole waves. We further show that the same out-of-plane THz pulse can reversibly switch a double-$\mathbf q$ dipole wave between degenerate topological variants within a few picoseconds, while preserving its spatial modulation. This process is enabled by damping-assisted inertial switching, in which the THz pulse injects energy to drive large-angle polarization rotation across shallow barriers, while dissipation removes excess energy and traps the system in the reversed state. These results establish ferroelectric nanocapacitors as a simple platform for programmable polar topology and low-power, THz-speed control through dissipative dynamics.

title: QC-espresso: Brewing quality in proteomics
abstract: Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics has become a standard approach for high-throughput proteomics, with DIA-NN emerging as one of the most widely adopted data-analysis platforms. However, despite the detailed information available in DIA-NN output reports, proteomics researchers may lack a streamlined and reproducible approach for assessing acquisition quality, identification consistency, and quantitative reliability across experiments. QC-espresso addresses this need through an automated, report-centered quality-control workflow implemented in R and Quarto. The tool processes a DIA-NN report.parquet file together with the corresponding FASTA database and generates a structured HTML report containing plots, run-level statistics, and exportable summary tables. Application to three experimental datasets allowed the visualization of lower identification depth related to high contaminant content; a chromatographic transition accompanied by altered retention-time and peak-width behavior; and the co-occurrence of systematic mass-error bias with changes in precursor- and protein-level quantitative-quality metrics. QC-espresso can be executed directly in R or through a portable Windows distribution with a graphical launcher, with both modes using the same analytical modules and report-generation workflow. The resulting report provides a consistent record for local inspection and troubleshooting of quality-control metrics within individual DIA proteomics experiments. QC-espresso is freely available at https://github.com/lanfredig/QC-espresso_DIA.

title: Intermediate Phase Selectivity in ZSM-5 Zeolite Synthesis and Framework Aluminum Distribution
abstract: The current understanding of zeolite crystallization is still far from well understood. Herein, we show that the crystallization pathway of high-silica ZSM-5, one of the most industrially important zeolites, can be altered not only by the type of organic structure-directing agents (OSDAs) at a gel Si/Al ratio of 50 but also by the simultaneous use of Na+ and Cs+ ions as inorganic structure-directing agents (ISDAs).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PFOS and GenX Induce Mitochondrial Toxicity and Differentially Alter Respiratory Complex Activities in Liver and Brain
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants associated with adverse health effects, yet the mitochondrial consequences of exposure to individual PFAS and their mixtures remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX) on mitochondrial respiratory complex activities under acute, sub-chronic, and chronic exposure conditions.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Control Enables Regulated Growth of Functional Metal–Phenolic Network Films
abstract: Metal–phenolic network (MPN) films are of widespread interest because of their potential application in biotechnology, catalysis, and the environment. Their formation typically involves the supramolecular assembly of phenolic ligands and metal ions from solution onto a solid substrate. Such assembly has been conducted exclusively from a single-phase solution, thus limiting spatiotemporal control over coordination and/or the range of precursors that can be used, and thereby restricting the compositional and structural diversity, as well as functionality, of MPN films.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: ILR-SMO: Iterative Latent Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration
abstract: Spatial multi-omics technologies jointly profile diverse molecular modalities with spatial context, providing a comprehensive view of cellular heterogeneity and tissue organization. To integrate spatial multi-omics data and identify spatial domains, a wide range of unsupervised methods has been proposed. However, recent approaches rely on single-step fusion, directly aggregating heterogeneous modalities into a shared representation, making embeddings sensitive to modality imbalance and measurement noise that are inherent to spatial multi-omics data, as well as unstable optimization under weak supervision. Here, we propose ILR-SMO (Iterative Latent Refinement for Spatial Multi-Omics), a unified self-supervised framework that reformulates multimodal integration as a stability-aware refinement process over a shared latent representation. Instead of single-step plain fusion, ILR-SMO progressively integrates modality-specific information through sequential updates, allowing information to be injected in a controlled manner. This incremental refinement enables later updates to correct or compensate for earlier deviations, resulting in more stable and robust representation learning under heterogeneous and noisy modalities. ILR-SMO further incorporates reliability-aware modality gating for adaptive modulation of modality contributions, and employs a joint objective to enforce spatial coherence while preventing representation collapse. Extensive experiments on five spatial multi-omics benchmarks demonstrate that ILR-SMO consistently outperforms seven state-of-the-art methods and exhibits strong robustness across diverse settings.

title: Beyond Direct Binding: Serotonin Rewires Model Brain Plasma Membrane-Mediated Communication Pathways in Y4R
abstract: Serotonin, an endogenous neurotransmitter, modulates pancreatic polypeptide (PP) recognition by the neuropeptide Y4 receptor (Y4R), a mechanism relevant to altered serotonergic signaling associated with metabolic disorder and anxiety. Although recent experiment demonstrates serotonin modulated PP dissociation kinetics of Y4R through membrane allostery, the molecular mechanism of serotonin induced lipidomic reorganization of the brain plasma membrane (BPM) relevant for Y4R activation is unknown. To this end, a total of 825.9 ns long all atom molecular dynamics simulations at 310 K elucidate the concentration-dependent coupling between serotonin partitioning, selective lipid reorganization, and PP binding and Y4R activation relevant intra-receptor communication in a heterogeneous, asymmetric model BPM. In the absence of serotonin, Y4R preferentially associates with the anionic lipids. Serotonin preferentially localizes at the lipid water interface over the PP binding and activation-associated regions of Y4R. At 6 mM, serotonin preferentially contacts phosphocholine species depleted from Y4R, whereas at 50 mM, phosphatidylinositol 4,5 bisphosphate dominates both microenvironments. These changes align with the selective remodeling of lipid networks, enhanced lipid chain ordering, and modest bilayer compaction. Weighted implementation of suboptimal paths analysis reveals concentration-dependent reorganization of communication pathways between experimentally implicated PP binding and activation associated Y4R residues. Collectively, these findings connects serotonin dependent selective lipid redistribution to altered intramolecular communication between Y4R residues associated with PP binding and G-protein coupling, and provide a framework for future experiments investigating membrane-mediated neuromodulation and neuronal signaling. These findings provide a basis for exploring lipid-targeted pharmacology as a complementary strategy to modulate GPCR allostery by altering membrane composition rather than directly targeting the receptor.

title: Synergistic Catalysis of Single-Site Rhenium and Ruthenium Nanoclusters for Ammonia Synthesis under Mild Conditions
abstract: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework.

title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
abstract: Event-related potentials (ERP) may reveal residual cognitive processing in disorders of consciousness, but clinical translation is limited because group-level effects do not guarantee reliable single-subject detection. Few ERP paradigms have been benchmarked in healthy participants and compared directly with patients in disorders of consciousness. We tested a hierarchical ERP battery in healthy controls and patients in minimally conscious state (MCS) to (1) estimate upper-bound single-subject detectability in healthy participants, (2) compare detection rates with those of MCS patients, and…

title: Kinetic Multi-reaction Model of Platinum Nanoparticle Oxidation and Cathodic Dissolution in a Wide Potential Window
abstract: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.

title: Constant-pH Molecular Dynamics Rationalizes Photoinduced Decarboxylation in Fluorescent Proteins
abstract: Many advanced imaging techniques, such as super-resolution microscopy, rely on photoinduced transformations of fluorescent proteins. In photoinduced decarboxylation, light absorption triggers loss of CO 2 from an acidic residue near the chromophore, often accompanied by a change in chromophore protonation that switches the protein to a fluorescent form, as in PA-GFP. Evidence from proteins in which this reaction has been observed indicates that the decarboxylating residue must be present in its deprotonated form.

title: Synthesis and Engineering of Bio-Based Porous Organic Polymers for Gold Recovery
abstract: The development of functional porous materials from renewable resources offers a promising strategy to reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks and advance sustainable materials technologies. Here, we report the facile synthesis of bio-based porous organic polymers (bioPOPs) through the polycondensation of vanillin-derived organic dialdehydes and inexpensive diamine monomers.

title: From Photo-crosslinking to Covalent: A Cascade DNA-Encoded Library Strategy for Pin1 Inhibitor Discovery
abstract: Peptidyl-prolyl cis–trans isomerase NIMA-interacting 1 (Pin1) plays vital biological roles in vivo and has been studied as a therapeutic target for a variety of human diseases. Covalent inhibitors represent the mainstream strategy in current Pin1 drug discovery, however, existing covalent molecules still rely on known affinity scaffolds or direct screening. Herein, we developed an innovative cascade DNA-encoded library (DEL) strategy that integrates photo-crosslinking with covalent targeting, enabling the de novo design of novel Pin1 covalent inhibitors.

title: Impact of Electrochemical Doping on the Excited State Decay of 2H-MoSe 2 Nanosheets
abstract: Colloidal 2H-MoSe 2 nanosheets combine solution processability with electronic properties attractive for photocatalytic water splitting, yet the electrochemical stability of the excited state remains poorly understood. We combine potential-modulated absorption spectroscopy and complementary electrochemical methods with transient absorption spectroscopy to investigate charge injection and excited-state dynamics in few-layer 2H-MoSe 2 nanosheet films.

title: Dataset of magnetic properties, structure and synthesis of doped barium and strontium M-type hexaferrites
abstract: M-type barium and strontium hexaferrites are the most widely produced permanent-magnet materials, and their structural and magnetic properties are commonly tuned by cationic substitution. The experimental data on doped hexaferrites are dispersed over hundreds of articles and reported with heterogeneous notation, units and descriptors. Here we present HexaMagDB, a manually curated dataset of 4388 records extracted from 662 peer-reviewed articles on doped Ba-and Sr-based M-type hexaferrites.

title: Insights into the formation of 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol in Cannabis sativa flowers through the identification of its glutathionylated and cysteinylated precursors
abstract: Odor emissions from cannabis cultivation have been described as “skunky”, a sensory characteristic recently associated with the compound 3-methylbut-2-ene-1-thiol (3MBT). However, the biosynthetic origin of this key odor-active compound in Cannabis sativa remains unknow. This study investigated the occurrence of the S-cysteine and S-glutathione conjugates of 3MBT (Cys-3MBT and GSH-3MBT) in CBD- and THC- dominant cannabis flowers and proposed them as possible precursor of the odor-thiol 3MBT.

title: Functional characterization of a hyperthermophilic glycyl radical enzyme reveals a reductive glycerol pathway in archaea
abstract: The function of the glycyl radical enzyme (GRE) PFL2 from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Archaeoglobus fulgidus has remained unresolved since its discovery. Structural and sequence analyses initially suggested that PFL2 was a B12-independent glycerol dehydratase (GDHt), whereas subsequent structural and transcriptional evidence implicated it as a methylalkylsuccinate synthase involved in anaerobic alkane activation. Difficulties in reconstituting active PFL2 in vitro prevented either assignment from being established biochemically.

title: 18 O-Informed Metabolomics Reveals Microbial Phosphoryl-Transfer Dynamics and Stress-Induced Changes
abstract: Microbial metabolism provides critical ecosystem functions, yet characterizing microbial metabolic activity in environmental systems remain challenging. Since phosphoryl-transfer reactions are central to energy metabolism, biosynthesis, and metabolic regulation, they have been proposed as a proxy for overall metabolic activity. Some phosphoryl-transfer reactions are known to contribute to the oxygen isotope fractionation between phosphate and water, leaving an isotopic signature of metabolic activity.

title: Pressure-Induced Formation of Intermetallic CrBi2
abstract: Binary transition-metal bismuth compounds offer a new class of solid-state materials with emergent properties such as magnetism, superconductivity, thermoelectricity and nontrivial topology. Under ambient conditions, Bi shows immiscibility with many other elements. High-pressure can offers an alternative thermodynamic landscape for Bi-based intermetallic systems. Herein, we computationally explore the energy landscape for the immiscible Cr-Bi systems under high-pressure.

title: A linear-scaling explicitly correlated local natural orbital CCSD(T) approach
abstract: We introduce an integral-direct, linear-scaling, local explicitly correlated (F12) coupled-cluster (CC) singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)] approach building on our established local natural orbital (LNO) CCSD(T) [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2018, 14, 4193] and local second-order Møller–Plesset F12 [J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2026, 22, 2946] techniques. By generating and transforming all the required integrals on-the-fly, the algorithm eliminates integral storage requirements, resulting in asymptotically constant memory usage and negligible disk I/O.

title: Squaramide-based ultrasensitive and reversible colourimetric dual sensor for the detection of copper and metal-ion-assisted acetate anion
abstract: A tripodal squaramide–quinoline– tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (TREN) chemosensor, TSQAQ, was synthesised in good yield using diethylsquarate, 8-aminoquinoline and tris(2aminoethyl)amine as starting materials. The chemosensor was evaluated as a dual-mode colorimetric platform for the selective naked-eye detection of Cu2+ in DMSO and Cd2+ (precursor was cadmium acetate, CA) in acetonitrile.

title: Coupling kinetic and techno-economic models reveals hidden biodesign targets
abstract: Metabolic and bioprocess engineering aim to achieve high fermentation titer, rate and yield (TRY), yet no general framework connects these interdependent metrics to facility-scale economics. We introduce NSKinetics, an agile computational framework embedding biochemically structured kinetic models within facility-scale process simulation, techno-economic analysis, uncertainty analysis, global sensitivity analysis, and optimization.

title: Multi-Scale Continuum Modeling of Mediated Electron Transfer in 3D Living Bio-Anodes
abstract: Bioelectrochemical systems, in which electroactive microbes transfer electrons across biological-abiotic interfaces, represent a vital technology for sustainable energy production, chemical synthesis, and environmental remediation. However, these systems are constrained by a two-dimensional design paradigm, with reactors achieving power densities 10–100-times lower than theoretical limits because conventional architectures restrict electron transfer to a single layer at the electrode surface.

title: ETALON: Verified Execution and Persistent Research Memory for Agentic Computer-Aided Drug Design
abstract: Language-model agents can coordinate computational drug discovery, but adapting a campaign to new evidence requires scientific software that supports flexible workflows, consistent modeling, and continuity across research sessions. Here we present ETALON, a harness that equips a general-purpose coding agent with an integrated environment for computer-aided drug design.

title: Influence of divalent cations on the adsorption of DNA origami nanostructures at TiO2 surfaces
abstract: The controlled adsorption of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) at oxides surfaces is an important step in many applications, ranging from lithographic patterning to sensor fabrication. It is usually facilitated by divalent cations, which screen electrostatic repulsion between the DONs and the surface and may even form salt bridges that firmly immobilize the adsorbed DONs. Here, we investigate DON adsorption at TiO2(110) surfaces mediated by Mg2+, Ca2+, and Sr2+.

title: Exploiting Carboxylate Effects to Enhance Cp*Co III -Catalyzed C–H Functionalization
abstract: Carboxylates are ubiquitous additives in Cp*Co III -catalyzed C–H functionalization, yet their influence on catalyst speciation and catalytic performance remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that carboxylate choice can markedly improve reaction efficiency, particularly for substrates bearing weakly coordinating directing groups. Combining high-throughput experimentation (HTE) and reaction optimization, we identified mesitoic acid (MesCO 2 H) as an effective additive for hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), outperforming conventional carboxylates.

title: A Zwitterionic Indylene with Ambiphilic Redox Reactivity
abstract: Extending transition-metal-like organometallic redox chemistry to indium remains a challenge in molecular main-group chemistry. Here, we report a zwitterionic indylene supported by an anionic bis(N-heterocyclic carbene)borate ligand that displays diverse redox reactivity. Computational and structural analyses reveal a relatively narrow HOMO–LUMO gap together with a stabilizing arene–In interaction involving a vacant indium p orbital, endowing the In(I) centre with complementary donor and acceptor character.

title: Formation Energy is All You Need
abstract: A Pourbaix diagram maps which species of an element (metal, ion, oxide or hydroxide) is thermodynamically stable in water as a function of potential and pH, at fixed temperature, pressure and composition. Constructing one requires the Gibbs energies of formation of the participating phases and species. Obtaining reliable values, however, remains difficult: competing phases and species can differ by only a few kilojoules per mole, while published compilations may disagree and are not always freely reusable.

title: Surfactant-Toolkit and SurfBench-200: an open computation toolkit and a benchmark of tool-augmented language-model reasoning in surfactant science
abstract: Language models are increasingly used as research assistants in chemistry, but their quantitative work insurfactantscience hasnotbeen measured.We introduce Surfactant-Toolkit, an MIT-licensed Python library and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with 123 validated tools for micellization, mixed micelles, adsorption, emulsions, micelle structure and transport,andSurfBench-200,200graduate-levelquestionswhosereferenceanswersare computed by the toolkit and graded field by field by deterministic scripts.

title: Redox-Active Leaving Group Enables the Deoxygenative Arylation of Unactivated Aliphatic Alcohols by Thermal, Homogeneous Iron(I)-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling
abstract: Aliphatic alcohols were installed with proposed leaving groups for reaction with well defined, 1,3-diketiminesupported (NacNac)iron(I)-(η6-PhMe) metalloradical, indicating a redox-active 2-isoquinolinyl ether substrate to undergo reductive homolytic C(sp3)–O bond cleavage concomitant with alkyl radical generation as determined by PBN spin trap. The optimal isoquinolinyl ether was employed as substrate in Kumada cross-coupling catalyzed by 10 mol% (NacNac)iron(II) chloride, yielding the deoxygenated, arylated product following homolytic C(sp3)–O β-scission.

title: Construction of a Curated Literature Dataset and Machine Learning-Guided Exploration of Supported Metal Catalysts for Low- to Intermediate-Temperature Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
abstract: Literature-derived results on reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) catalysts contain extensive information about catalyst design, yet their fragmentation makes systematic, data-driven exploration difficult. Here, we establish a framework that connects a curated RWGS literature dataset to interpretable machine-learning (ML) models and a flexible catalyst-search algorithm. We compiled 607 experimental records from 42 publications on supported metal and metal oxide catalysts evaluated at 300–450 °C, integrating catalyst compositions, preparation and reaction conditions, and CO yields.

title: Intermeshed Diphenylacetylenes with Axial Rotation Restricted by Intramolecular Donor–Acceptor Interactions
abstract: Diphenylacetylene (DPA) rotates almost freely around the acetylene axis with rotation mainly restricted by steric repulsion or covalent tethers. We report intermeshed diphenylacetylenes, in which bent π-conjugated units attached to DPA termini cause two donor–acceptor pairs to overlap with each other on opposite sides of the axis. Density functional theory calculations showed that a twisted, stacked conformation with a 36–40° dihedral angle was the most stable for all four molecules. The estimated P/M interconversion barriers (12.8–21.4 kcal/mol) increased with donor and acceptor strength.

title: Machine learning prediction of hydrogen sorption properties of zirconium-titanium based C14 Laves phase AB 2 alloy from chemical composition
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models were developed to predict the hydrogen sorp-tion properties of Zr–Ti-based C14 Laves phase AB 2 alloys—unit cell volume (V14), enthalpy of hydrogen absorption (∆H), entropy of hydrogen absorption (∆S), and equilibrium plateau pressure (P eq)—from chemical composition and calculated physical properties. A curated dataset of 244 alloys was compiled from the literature, with two feature categories compared: element atomic percent and properties-based variables (molar mass, bulk density, molar volume, atomic radius ratio, bulk modulus, electron density, B/A ratio).

title: Integrative single cell and machine learning analysis identifies fibroblast centric hub genes and therapeutic candidates in lung adenocarcinoma and ischemic cardiomyopathy
abstract: BackgroundIschemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined.MethodsWe integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes.

title: Tellurium–Oxygen Molecules Bridging MFI Zeolite Nanoplates into a b -Oriented Membrane for CO2 Separation
abstract: The orientation of zeolite pores parallel to gas transport can facilitate rapid selective gas separation; however, the fabrication of oriented zeolite membranes remains a grand challenge. This study reports a unique strategy of molecularly bridging zeolite nanoplates to fabricate a b-oriented MFI membrane for CO2 gas separation. Tellurium alkoxide of Te(C3H6O2)2 is designed as the bridging agent, and the MFI zeolite nanoplate is synthesized in the aspect ratio of ∼14 as the building block.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Split Intein Enables Ultralarge Dual-Phage Display for Drug Discovery
abstract: Phage display, a powerful ligand discovery technology, is limited by library capacity, with practical diversity typically ∼109 variants. This bottleneck stems from each phage requiring individual host cell propagation, making ultralarge libraries (1012–1014) impractical due to massive cell/culture volume demands. We introduce X-phage, a dual-phage display system using split-intein-mediated ligation to combine two genetically distinct phages into a single functional entity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: High-Efficiency Multistimuli Responsive Carbon Dots with Near-100% Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Anticounterfeiting Technologies
abstract: With the rising demand for information security and anticounterfeiting, developing intelligent luminescent materials responsive to external stimuli is crucial for enhancing encryption and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, a facile one-pot solvothermal strategy was developed to prepare multistimuli responsive carbon dots (CDs), which exhibit solvent-responsive, concentration-responsive, and pH-responsive properties, along with a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) approaching 100% in aqueous dispersion. Systematic investigations reveal that the high PLQY of the CDs originates from the cross-arranged nonextended conjugation of perylene-based backbones in the CDs core, which prevent further π–π stacking. In addition, surface functional groups regulate solvent-dependent luminescence behavior through polar interactions and hydrogen bonding. As the concentration increased, enhanced intermolecular interactions induce the emission from monomer-dominated to aggregate-dominated states. Furthermore, under different pH conditions, reversible protonation and deprotonation of surface functional groups enable dynamic modulation of the electronic structure, thereby regulating the fluorescence emission. By combining with polymers, multicolor high-brightness polymer powders with PLQY approaching 100% were successfully prepared. These composite materials demonstrate excellent performance in handicraft decoration and anticounterfeiting systems. This work not only provides a theoretical basis for the design of highly efficient luminescent CDs but also expands their potential in intelligent materials and photonic applications.

title: Swapping O for S: Converting Oxetanes into Thietanes and their Oxidized Derivatives
abstract: Thietanes, often considered as “oxetane analogs”, offer complementary physicochemical properties and, along with their oxidized derivatives, are attracting increasing interest in medicinal chemistry. Their exploration, however, remains limited, partly due to the restricted availability and structural diversity of appropriate building blocks. The variety of methods available for preparing oxetanes with diverse substitution patterns makes their conversion into thietanes an appealing strategy for both building-block synthesis and late-stage diversification.

title: Design and Benchmarking of CK2α′-Preferring Inhibitors for Huntington’s Disease: The Limits of Structure-Based Isoform Selectivity
abstract: Protein kinase CK2 acts through two catalytic isoforms, CK2α (A1) and CK2α′ (A2), whose ATP-binding sites differ at only two hinge positions, making isoform-selective inhibition difficult. We tested whether a standard structure-based pipeline can design and rank CK2α′-preferring compounds. In a paired benchmark of 140 compounds measured against both isoforms, none of the five docking-derived criteria, computed with GNINA and convolutional neural network rescoring, correlated with measured selectivity (ρ = −0.19 to +0.12), and for matched pairs differing by a single linker methylene, the…

title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
abstract: Language models increasingly serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as “The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is”, a small general-purpose model may answer “the alkyne group” instead of an alkyl fluoride. The output alone cannot tell whether the model failed to recognize the fluorine or recognized it and failed to say so.

title: Collision Cross Section Measurement within a Time-of-Flight Mass Analyzer
abstract: A proportion of ions travelling through a time-of-flight analyzer inevitably suffer collisions with background gas, resulting in unwanted transmission losses. As collision probability depends upon the ions’ collision cross section, it has been considered that measurement of ion transmission with variation of pressure, or flight path in the case of some multi-reflection analyzers, allows cross section to be determined. A theoretical model is presented, and practical evaluations performed upon a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer.

title: Uptake is cheap, breach is not: an ATP budget for nanoplastic–membrane interaction
abstract: Mechanical action of plastic particles on the cell membrane is repeatedly proposed as a route to cellular damage and to depletion of ATP, but the energy budget of that route has never been evaluated. Here I assemble it from four channels and from measured membrane constants. The bending work of engulfing one spherical particle is 8πκ ≈ 503 kBT ≈ 26 ATP and is independent of particle radius.

title: Integrating artificial intelligence and molecular simulation for peptide discovery: limitations, validation and decision-centered workflows
abstract: Summary. Therapeutic peptides occupy a chemical and pharmacological space between smallmolecules and biologics, offering extended recognition surfaces and access to targets that resist conventionalmodalities. Their discovery, however, requires the simultaneous optimization of activity, selectivity, stability, permeability and synthetic feasibility across a conformationally complex and chemically heterogeneous search space.

title: Benchmarking ReleaseKinetix: Numerical Equivalence of a Web-Based Platform for Dissolution Analytics and Regulatory Decision Support
abstract: Before innovative computational instruments are incorporated into regulatory research and scientific practice, a thorough presentation of their computational reproducibility is fundamental. This study thoroughly benchmarks ReleaseKinetix. ReleaseKinetix is an independent, browserbased platform. It is used for comparison of in vitro dissolution profiles and release-kinetic modeling. The study benchmarks ReleaseKinetix (for comparing in vitro dissolution profiles and modeling release kinetics) against two independently written nonlinear least-squares reference engines.

title: When the standard is not the standard
abstract: A calibration standard can satisfy the chromatographic system suitability parameters monitored in routine use and still be an order of magnitude from its nominal concentration. This report documents two such events in a single method development exercise on coenzyme Q10 (ubidecarenone), together with the solubility measurements that explain them. A stock solution prepared at 1 mg/mL in methanol:ethanol 65:35 (v/v) — approximately five times the equilibrium solubility of coenzyme Q10 in that diluent — was forced into solution by sonication and warming to approximately 36–37 °C, then held…

title: Architected Iron-Carbon and Stainless-Steel Electrodes Fabricated by Additive Manufacturing for All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: All-iron redox flow batteries are attractive candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their use of earth-abundant and low-cost active materials. In this work, additively manufactured architected electrodes were developed to investigate the influence of electrode composition and architecture on cell performance. Stainless-steel electrodes were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion, while iron-containing carbon (Fe-C) electrodes were fabricated by digital light processing followed by carbonization.

title: Completing the Jacob’s ladder of multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory with a doubly hybrid functional
abstract: Here we introduce MC-xDH5, the first doubly hybrid functional within the multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory (MC-PDFT) framework, completing the top rung of the MC-PDFT Jacob’s ladder. Introducing perturbative correlation into MC-PDFT raises two challenges: double counting and reference selection. MC-xDH5 overcomes both through the cross-entropy of the natural orbital occupations, which subtracts an estimate of the correlation already contained in the reference and defines a saturation active space (SAS) for the perturbative step.

title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
abstract: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the labo- ratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a framework for self-evolving laboratories (SEL), connecting computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs.

title: Comparative Magnetic Heating of Surface-Modified Ferrite Nanoparticles in Water and Agar Phantoms
abstract: This study compares the alternating-magnetic-field (AMF) heating of Fe3O4-, MnFe2O4-, MgFe2O4-, and SrFe12O19-targeted nanoparticle preparations and of their sequentially silica-modified, aminated, Aufunctionalized, and PEG-treated forms. The compositions are identified by their nominal synthesis precursors. Temperature–time curves and the times required to reach 42 °C were measured in water and in nominally 1% agar phantoms under identical induction-generator settings (132 kHz; 5 kW rated output).

title: Design Of Earth-Abundant W(0) Complexes For Near-Infrared Absorbance Via Ligand Optimization
abstract: This work focuses on developing new earth-abundant metal complexes to be used as eAicient near-infrared (NIR) absorbers and photosensitizers for applications in photocatalysis, bioimaging, and photodynamic therapy. By modifying ligand types coordinated to a W(0) center, we aim to enhance NIR absorption and reduce nonradiative decay pathways in turn. Through collaboration with experimentalists in Dr. Wenfang Sun’s group, they were able to synthesize new W(0) complexes coordinated with four carbonyl’s and one 2-(pyrid-2-yl)(benz)imidazole ligand.

title: Hydrogen-Bond Network-Enabled Access to Aryl Benzoiodoxolones via Mild, HFIP-Mediated Boron-Iodane Exchange
abstract: We report here a boron-iodane exchange reaction that occurs between aryl boronic acids and 1-hydroxybenzoiodoxoles at extremely mild conditions, that is without the need for using strong Lewis acids or pyrophoric/toxic reagents. Our approach enables selective arylation of a variety of 1-hydroxybenzoiodoxolones with electronically-diverse aromatic boronic acids that is facilitated only by hydrogen-bond donating HFIP, eventually giving rise to a wide range of 1-arylbenzoiodoxolones in good to excellent yields.

title: Highly tunable artificial Suzukiase catalyzes the atroposelective synthesis of N -heterobiaryls
abstract: Enantiopure N -heterobiaryls are valuable motifs in medicinal chemistry and asymmetric catalysis. Yet, their atroposelective synthesis via Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling remains challenging as Lewis-basic heterocycles can coordinate to the Pd catalyst and inhibit catalysis. Herein, we report an artificial Suzukiase based on a biotinylated dialkylbiarylphosphine-Pd cofactor embedded within a streptavidin scaffold (Sav).

title: Cobalt Photocatalyzed Carbonylation Reactions in Flow: From Mass-Transfer to Light-Limited Regimes
abstract: Photocatalytic carbonylation has emerged as a powerful approach for the synthesis of carboxylic acid derivatives under mild reaction conditions. However, translating these transformations to industrially relevant scales remains a significant challenge because reaction performance is intrinsically linked to e?icient photon delivery and gas–liquid mass transfer.

title: checkSI: Computer-Assisted Pre-Submission Checking of Characterization Data for Organic Compounds
abstract: Characterization records in organic chemistry link a compound's name with its NMR, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) and, where available, elemental analysis data. These values are often transferred manually into the Supporting Information (SI). An analysis of Organic Letters SI files found errors of concern in about one in ten compounds with accurate mass data. Here we present checkSI, an open-source tool that checks reporting conventions and consistency among characterization fields. It reads SI files and manuscripts in text-based PDF or Word (DOCX) format.

title: A Ligand-Centered Radical Reveals Orbital-Specific Bonding Differences Between Near-Isoradial Transuranium-Actinide and Lanthanide Complexes
abstract: Understanding how metal-ligand covalency evolves across the actinide series and compared to the lanthanide series remains a central challenge in f-element chemistry because subtle changes in both the energies and radial extension of the 5f and 6d orbitals can profoundly influence chemical bonding. Here, we employ a redox-active bipyridyl ligand platform to isolate trivalent actinide and lanthanide complexes of the form Cp* 2MIII(tBu2bipy•−) (1-M; Cp* = pentamethylcyclopentadienide; tBu2bipy•− = 4,4′-di-tert-butyl-2,2′-bipyridine radical anion; M = An = Np, Pu; M = Ln = La, Ce, Pr), including…

title: Surface Reconstruction Activates Bridge Sites of Rutile IrO2(110) for Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: IrO2 is the state-of-the-art catalyst for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acid. Previous theoretical investigations are largely based on the (110) surface, with undercoordinated Ircus sites being considered as active centers under reaction conditions, whereas coordinated Irbr sites are considered spectators. Using a combination of density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics, we demonstrate that the Irbr sites reconstruct under anodic polarization leading to the formation of single-atom catalyst (SAC)-like centers.

title: Mechanistic Monte Carlo assessment of colocalized permeation enhancement and efflux modulation for oral peptide delivery
abstract: The oral absolute bioavailability of 2- to 4-kDa peptides remains near 1%. We constructed a mechanistic Monte Carlo model of a colocalized, reversible permeation-enhancer and efflux-modulator architecture (Dual-Lock) with explicit mass balances and evidence-graded, correlated priors and asked when it would increase bioavailability to at least 4% with predicted reversible epithelial exposure. The arms shared random draws so that the ablations and negative controls isolated each component.

title: Electrochemical Insights into Histatin 5 Antimicrobial Activity: Cu(II) Redox Chemistry and Model Lipid Layer Interactions
abstract: Histatin 5 (Hst5) is one of the most potent antifungal members of the salivary histatin family, exhibiting activity against the opportunistic fungus Candida albicans, with reported intracellular localisation to mitochondria and effects on mitochondrial function. This localization, together with Hst5's ability to bind redox-active Cu(II) ions, suggested that Cu(II)-Hst5 complexes could catalyze ROS production via Cu(II)/Cu(I) cycling.

title: Linkage-sparing Assembly of Single-crystalline Phenylene-linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Crystallising two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) from irreversible bonds is hindered by the absence of error correction and out-of-plane disorder. Here, we establish linkage-sparing assembly (LSA) as a novel strategy for overcoming this limitation: preformed oligomeric motifs encode part of the target lattice, reducing the number of new irreversible C–C bonds required for framework growth. Combined with kinetic control through temperature and water content, LSA yields micrometre-scale single crystals of a phenylene-linked COF (HPPCOF) formed by ketone cyclotrimerisation.

title: EXAFS probing of nonequilibrium solvation dynamics of nascent halogen radicals
abstract: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy can be used to observe the local environment around absorber atoms. Provided high enough time resolution can be achieved, this would open the possibility of tracking nonequilibrium solvation dynamics in photoreactions in real time. Here we simulate an electron detachment process from aqueous Cl−, Br−, and I− using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics molecular dynamics simulations and analyze the following solvation dynamics.

title: Ion Transport Dynamics in Poly(ethylene oxide) and Poly(pentyl malonate) Electrolytes for Lithium Batteries
abstract: The rate at which batteries can be charged is limited by the transport of the working ion through the electrolyte. In polymer electrolytes, the selective transport of Li+ ions is dependent on the solvation cage surrounding the Li+ ion. In this work, we measure cation and anion self-diffusion coefficients using pulsed field gradient nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (PFG-NMR) in electrolytes containing poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) or poly(pentyl malonate) (PPM) mixed with lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI).

title: Near‑Zero Energy CO2 Capture Using Vapour Assisted Phase Swing Adsorption (VAPSA)
abstract: Microporous materials are promising adsorbents for gas separations, but their adoption has been limited by the energy requirements of vacuum or heat used to regenerate the material. Lower energy swing triggers have been explored (such as light, magnetism, electricity, and humidity) to desorb gases; however, these alternative processes can also use large amounts of energy at scale. Hydrogen bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) are molecular microporous materials that exhibit solution processibility and polymorphism.

title: Emergent Pressure-Induced Reactivity of 4,4’-Azopyridine-Templated Hybrid Metal Oxides
abstract: We show that the ordered installation of 4,4’-azopyridine ligands featuring reactive azo groups within layered hybrid inorganic–organic metal oxides produces enhanced pressure-induced reactivity relative to the molecular compound alone or previously reported hybrids. Using in situ X-ray diffraction measurements along with vibrational and optical spectroscopies, as well as ex situ neutron elastic and inelastic scattering, vibrational, solid-state NMR, and EPR spectroscopies and mass spectrometry, we examine the structural and electronic evolution of both organic and inorganic components under…

title: Transcending the Beer–Lambert Limit with Full-Dimensional Digital Colorimetry
abstract: Automated workflows are rapidly accelerating discovery across the chemical sciences, yet the throughput of such platforms remains bottlenecked by the high cost and slow operation of traditional analytical hardware. 1 While digital colorimetry offers a ubiquitous, low-cost alternative for reaction monitoring, current techniques rely on the linear approximations of the Beer–Lambert law. 2, 3 This constraint causes data degeneracy, severely limiting analytical accuracy.

title: Auditing frozen chemical language model embeddings for drug-delivery screening: fingerprint baselines, random-initialization controls, and scaffold-memorization control tasks
abstract: Frozen embeddings from pretrained chemical language models (cLMs) are widely used as features for ADMET and drug-delivery prediction, often with a linear probe and little validation of what the representation actually contributes. We audit two small public cLMs (ChemBERTa-77M-MLM and ChemBERTa-77M-MTR, 3.4M parameters each) on three delivery-relevant endpoints from openly licensed sources: blood–brain barrier penetration (B3DB, CC0), PAMPA permeability (NCATS via PubChem), and Caco-2 permeability (OpenADMET, CC-BY-4.0).

title: Warm Isostatic vs. Cold Uniaxial Pressing in All-Solid-State Battery Cathodes: Linking Microstructure, Transport, and Mechano-Electrochemical Response
abstract: Lithium-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are attracting increasing attention as nextgeneration energy storage systems. However, maintaining intimate solid–solid contact within NMC-based composite cathodes during repeated lithium extraction and insertion remains a major challenge. Because the stability of these contacts is largely determined by the electrode microstructure established during manufacturing, advanced pressing strategies are increasingly being explored to reduce residual porosity and promote homogeneous particle packing.

title: Analytical Evidence for Assessing Plastic Pyrolysis Oils as Steam Cracker Feedstocks
abstract: Qualification of plastic pyrolysis oils for steam cracking requires measurements that connect product recovery, composition, and operating performance. This critical narrative review examines 96 selected full-text publications through reconstructed comparisons of analytical coverage, calibration, uncertainty, and material inventories. In individual studies, GC-assigned species represented approximately 11% of total silicon, and olefin estimates differed by 7.4 percentage points despite a pooled coefficient of determination above 0.99.

title: Transformation of Nitrogenous Compounds in Water Microdroplets
abstract: Microdroplets drive small-molecule activation reactions that are difficult in bulk solution. Recent studies have demonstrated that microdroplets activate inert N2 under ambient conditions to generate multiple nitrogencontaining compounds. However, there are still many controversial issues regarding the transformation of nitrogencontaining compounds in water microdroplets. Here, we combine online high-resolution mass spectrometry on two instrument platforms with 15N and 18O labeling to investigate nitrogen-containing species in pneumatically generated water microdroplets.

title: Decision stability of a default docking pipeline: a seed, box-placement, and protomer audit on LIT-PCBA MTORC1
abstract: Agentic and automated drug-discovery workflows increasingly call molecular docking as a black-box subroutine and act on its ranked output, typically from a single run under software defaults. We ask a narrow, operational question: if the same default pipeline is re-run with a different random seed, a slightly displaced search box, or a different input protomer, which decisions-the top-k compounds a downstream agent would advanceactually change?

title: From Dynamic Frustration to Steric Trapping: The Microscopic Mechanism of a Monotropic Phase Transition
abstract: The atomic-level mechanisms governing solvent-driven single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) topotactic transitions are notoriously difficult to capture, as transient, symmetry-broken intermediates (Z′ > 1) rarely survive structural collapse. Here, we map the complete molecular trajectory of a cooperative solid-state transition within a heavily hydrated di-iron-µ-O-2'-cytidine monophosphate complex, [Fe2(µ-O)(TPA)2(2′-CMP)](ClO4)2·xH2O.

title: Revealing the role of Li content on the structural stability of textured LiCoO 2 battery electrodes along fast diffusing <11x> directions
abstract: Facile ion transport in layered battery cathode systems require (11x) terminating facets. However, the facets that provide accelerated transport also amplify deleterious phase transitions and chemical reactions. The coupling between initial intercalant ion content (nominal lithium-ion stoichiometry), ionic mobility and phase transformations along the fastest diffusing facets remain understudied.

title: Incorporating Polarization into ML/MM Endpoint Calculations for Protein–Ligand Affinity Ranking
abstract: Endpoint free-energy calculations combine low computational cost with reasonable accuracy and are widely used to rank protein–ligand affinities, yet describing charge polarization in these calculations remains a challenge. Here we introduce a machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) framework that incorporates polarizationcorrected mechanical embedding (PCME) and electrostatic embedding (EE) into endpoint calculations, using binding-state-and conformation-dependent ML charges in both the gas-phase energy and polar solvation terms.

title: Randomized PEG-Based Polycarbonate Micelles with PEG-like Stealth Properties and Biodistribution
abstract: The increase in anti-PEG antibodies (APAs) as well as PEG-related adverse effects have questioned the benefits of PEGylated nanotherapeutics. Growing awareness of the safety and efficacy of PEGylation has prompted research into countermeasures, including alternative polymers. Among these, randomized PEG (rPEG) was established as a fundamentally new approach that preserves the polyether structure while preventing antibody recognition through isomerization. Here, rPEG was incorporated into polymeric micelles (PMs) for immunodrug delivery to assess its suitability as a PEG replacement.

title: Bringing coupled‑cluster theory to the strong-correlation frontier
abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular electronic energies is essential yet remains challenging for strongly correlated systems, where conventional coupled-cluster (CC) methods break down. Here we present a generalized valence bond-based block-correlated coupled‑cluster (GVB-BCCC) framework to overcome this limitation. In contrast to standard CC approaches built upon a single-determinant reference, our method employs a multi‑determinantal GVB reference paired with a cluster operator that consistently captures both static and dynamic electron correlation effects, while retaining computational…

title: Literature-Scale Mössbauer Data Enable Prediction, Electronic-State Interpretation, and Chemical Insight in Molecular Iron Chemistry
abstract: Experimental spectroscopy is central to molecular characterization, yet conventional quantitative analysis often compresses rich structural and electronic information into a few calculated observables, leaving much of the experimental context and expert interpretation reported in the literature underused. Here, using molecular 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy as a representative case, we reconstructed more than 300 publications into FeMössDB, a site-resolved dataset containing 502 Fe complexes and 624 Fe sites with linked structural, experimental, and interpretive information.

title: The Evolution of Electronic Structure in Conjugated Molecules Revealed by Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory and Density-Based Analyses: II. Polyacenes
abstract: Large conjugated molecules feature small gaps between occupied and virtual orbital spaces, which results in complex electronic structure patterns in their low-lying states. These orbital near-degeneracies also challenge quantum chemistry methods. Mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT (MRSF-TDDFT) and density-matrix-based analyses provide useful tools to interrogate electronic structure in large conjugated molecules. This paper investigates one such family—polyacenes.

title: Integrating Generative AI and Data Science into General Chemistry Laboratories
abstract: The emergence of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini is reshaping research, education, and industry. Recent workforce data indicate a widening gap between declining junior-level opportunities and rising demand for senior-level expertise, underscoring the urgent need to adapt undergraduate chemistry curricula to prepare students for an AI-enabled workforce. To address this challenge, we designed a series of Python-based laboratory experiments for General Chemistry that integrate generative AI with instructor guidance to enhance student learning.

title: A Coupled Chemo-Mechanical and Life-Cycle Framework for Oyster-Shell-Derived Cementitious Materials in Aggressive Infrastructure Environments
abstract: Oyster-shell powder is promoted as a low-carbon cement substitute, but joint carbon and durability benefits are usually asserted rather than tested. This paper asks when shell-derived concrete (shell replacing cement) delivers a carbon cut with non-inferior service life relative to ordinary Portland cement (OPC) concrete. A coupled hydration–transport–damage–carbon model is run through paired Monte Carlo analysis of a pavement, a dam and a marine culvert. Published data reject the original inert-filler strength model.

title: Impedance, admittance or current–voltage? What each measurement really tells about charge transport in deepblue hosts
abstract: Host mobilities are usually quoted from one technique without saying what that technique can actually pin down. Using single-carrier devices of three deep-blue phosphine-oxide hosts, we credit impedance spectroscopy (IS), admittance and steady-state current–voltage (J–V ) data each with what they can fix. Documented rules for point selection, dispersion and transport onset make the published IS mobilities reproducible.

title: Beyond single numbers: how to choose host materials for deep-blue TADF OLEDs
abstract: Deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs stand or fall on their host, yet hosts are still chosen from a handful of single numbers: triplet energy, singlet–triplet gap, frontier levels, glass transition and carrier mobility. We compiled these descriptors for sixteen hosts and cohost components from six chemical families, tracing the source, method and condition behind every value, and find that most are protocol-dependent observables rather than material constants: published triplet energies of one molecule differ by up to 0.12 eV, and five analyses of the same devices…

title: Same Raw Data, Different Numbers: Locked Analysis Rules Make Film Descriptors of Organic Semiconductors Reproducible
