abstract: Optical gaps, Urbach energies, oxidation potentials, surface correlation lengths, diffraction order and thermal transitions are used to rank organic semiconductor films, yet each number is the output of an analysis whose discretionary steps are rarely fixed. Here a protocol card is introduced in which every descriptor is extracted by a locked rule and accepted only if it passes a stated test; otherwise it is reported as “not determined”. Each rule is stress-tested against the choices it fixes.

title: vibe-qc: expert-directed agentic engineering for scientific software development
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can implement scientific software, but useful development also requires executable comparisons, inspectable results and a record of scientific decisions. This case study examines the tooling that enables semi-autonomous electronic-structure software development under expert direction. VIBE-QC supplies molecular and periodic calculations; vibe-scheduler queues and manages calculations across clusters and a fleet of workstations; vibe-viewer and the Quantum Visualization Format (QVF) connect numerical outputs to portable inspection and reproducible…

title: The Meta-Link Rule Revisited: Relaxed Triplets and Non-Radiative Loss Decide Deep-Blue Phosphine-Oxide Hosts
abstract: Deep-blue host design relies on a textbook rule: join the donor and the phosphine-oxide acceptor through a meta-phenylene link to break conjugation and keep the triplet energy high. Tested against experiment, the rule alone does not explain the measured photoluminescence-yield ordering. In a prespecified test on 36 deep-blue emitters, none of the tested radiative descriptors passes all four film-yield ranking criteria, and the meta-linked S1 host and the para-linked S4 host have overlapping apparent radiative-rate brackets yet differ 18-fold in apparent non-radiative rate.

title: Colour-Stable When Heated, Colour-Shifting When Excited: Deep-Blue TADF Hosts Need Vector, Not Scalar, Screening
abstract: Deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials are screened by a single figure of meritquantum yield, singlet–triplet gap, colour shift or activation energy—on the assumption that a material robust under one stress is robust under others. Here we show that this assumption fails. For three related phosphineoxide hosts, the host whose emission colour moves least on heating is the one whose colour moves most when the excitation wavelength is changed: an 8-to 17-fold reversal, read directly from instrument chromaticity coordinates.

title: Microbial Pyrolysis for the Sustainable Synthesis of Nanoparticle-Embedded Carbon Electrocatalysts
abstract: Electrocatalytic processes are essential for a sustainable global economy, yet conventional catalyst synthesis often relies on hazardous reagents and insulating binders that impede performance. Here, microbial extracellular electron transfer for nanoparticle synthesis is integrated with the controlled pyrolysis of microbial monolayers to generate nanoparticle-embedded carbon electrodes.

title: Synthesis of N-Protected L-DOPA(acetonide) Derivatives
abstract: The modular synthesis of N-protected L-DOPA(acetonide) derivatives from readily available H-L-DOPA-OH is reported. A consecutive protecting group strategy and a partial hydrogenolytic removal affords H-L-DOPA(acetonide)-OH as key intermediate. Subsequent N-protection provides Fmoc-, Boc-, Cbz-, and Alloc-protected derivatives in excellent yields (95–99%). The key intermediate was further converted into the corresponding N-carboxyanhydride – a building block for polypeptide synthesis.

title: Electron Density of Delocalized Bonds from Correlated One-Particle Density Matrices
abstract: Extending bond-delocalization analysis to correlated one-particle density matrices requires separating fractional occupations from the projector structure underlying determinant-based algorithms. We define the electron density of delocalized bonds (EDDB) by combining bond-orbital projection (BOP) results for cumulative spectral projectors with occupation-gap weights. A structural bound on the raw BOP matrix ensures a positive semidefinite density layer bounded by its parent density.

title: Repurposing HIV Protease Inhibitors as Antifungal Chemosensitizers Against Multidrug Resistant Candida auris: Promise, Limitations, and Translational Challenges
abstract: Candidozyma auris (formerly known as Candida auris hereafter , C. auris ) is an emerging healthcare associated fungal pathogen. Which is associated with multidrug resistance, environmental persistence, and invasive infections in vulnerable patients. Reduced proneness to established antifungal agents has induced investigation of unorthodox strategies. One approach is antifungal chemosensitization, in which a compound with restricted or no direct antifungal activity enhances the effect of a prevailing antifungal.

title: An Audited Open Record of Three Deep-Blue TADF Host Materials with Benchmark Tasks for Machine Learning
abstract: We present an audited measurement record of three phosphine-oxide hosts for deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), with provenance metadata and benchmark tasks for machine learning. A scripted audit converted a 5276-file archive into 1662 files (1639 instrument files and 23 instrument-side fit tables) in ten record families, identifying 44 files stored under incorrect material or medium labels and retaining parsed settings, provenance tiers and quality flags.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Halogen Substitution in ortho-Benzoxy Phenylboronic Acid Catalysts for Amidation Reactions
abstract: Boronic acids have emerged as powerful catalysts for amidation reactions. Based on a previously identified orthobenzoxy phenylboronic acid motif, a systematic structure-activity study was performed. A catalyst library spanning F, Cl, Br, and I substitution on the ortho-benzoxy substituent was synthesized and evaluated as catalysts in amidation reactions. Catalytic activity increased in the order F < Cl < Br < I and followed the substitution pattern ortho < para < meta, with the meta-iodo derivative showing the highest conversion.

title: Materials Property Prediction with a Site-Resolved Three-Dimensional Voxel Convolution Neural Network
abstract: Identifying low-energy atomic arrangements is central to the design of multicomponent materials such as high-entropy cathodes and perovskites, but the number of possible arrangements grows combinatorially with the number of elements. Calculating each arrangement with density functional theory (DFT) is impractical, and many machine-learning models require relaxed structures that become available only after such calculations.

title: Biosynthesis of acyl-CoA thioesters from simple amines, alcohols and esters enabled by co-immobilized multi-enzyme systems
abstract: Acyl-Coenzyme A derivatives are a valuable family of metabolic intermediates with many applications, such as building blocks on biosynthetic routes, protein labeling, or potential therapeutics. However, their synthesis is limited to highly activated molecules (i.e. anhydrides) or carboxylic acids. In this work, we developed two multifunctional heterogeneous biocatalysts, capable of synthesizing acyl-CoA thioesters from primary alcohols or amines using free Coenzyme A via two different stepwise enzymatic cascades.

title: Negative effects of oxygen and halogen species on charge extraction in perovskite solar cells with fullerene electron transport layers
abstract: In this work, we explore the effect of small molecular species such as air, iodide, iodine, and triiodide species on the charge transport behavior of fullerene electron transport layers and the concomitant effects on performance and stability of perovskite solar cells. First, we show that without SnOx buffer layers, two-step vapor deposited perovskites have notable losses upon air exposure while spin-coated perovskites have minor losses.

title: Inverse magneto-ionics enhances oxygen evolution reaction
abstract: Applying magnetic fields to electrodes has been reported to enhance electrochemical reactions, leading to numerous studies and the hypothesis that externally applied magnetic fields manipulate direct spin exchange at the electrode–electrolyte interface to control reaction kinetics. However, a closer analysis suggests that this mechanism is unlikely to play a significant role, whereas the influence of magnetic gradient forces on ion migration is well established. Here, we provide experimental evidence supporting the latter mechanism for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on nickel.

title: Enantio-Complementary Synthesis of Atropisomeric C–N Biaryl Amines via Imine Reductase-Mediated Dynamic Kinetic Resolution
abstract: C–N axially chiral biaryl amines constitute privileged scaffolds in drug discovery and asymmetric catalysis, yet they remain synthetically challenging due to low rotational barriers and inherent conformational flexibility. While biocatalysis presents an attractive avenue for constructing chiral amines, the lack of mirror-image enzymes has historically limited access to all stereoisomers. Here, we develop an unconventional biocatalytic platform leveraging dynamic kinetic reductive amination to synthesize C–N axially chiral biaryl amines in both enantiomeric forms.

title: From a Tight-Binding Hessian to an AMBER Iron-Sulfur Site: A Rubredoxin Stress Test
abstract: Parameterized bonded metal sites represent the lowest cost option for molecular dynamics (MD) studies of metalloproteins. However, their quality depends entirely upon the underlying quantum computation and validation. Here, we have asked whether it is possible to generate reliable AMBER force field parameters for a rubredoxin Fe-S4 active site from an extended tight-binding (xTB-family) Hessian. The Hessian derived from a 49-atom cluster was projected using the Seminario method to give parameters for Fe-S and S-Fe-S interactions.

title: Macroscopic two-dimensional sheets by chemically triggered self-assembly.
abstract: Bottom-up self-assembly of two-dimensional (2D) sheets is rare. We present in situ reaction driven self-assembly for semithroughput synthesis of imine based 2D materials. Easily tuneable molecular structures and reaction kinetics allow for up to seven sheet forming systems.

title: COSMO-RS screening and experimental solid-liquid equilibrium validation of eutectic solvent candidates for CO2 capture
abstract: A combined computational -experimental strategy was applied to accelerate the identification of deep eutectic solvent (DES) candidates for CO 2 capture applications. A diverse group of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) and hydrogen bond donors (HBD) was selected and screened as potential DES constituents. Subsequently COSMO-RS was used to predict solid-liquid equilibrium (SLE) phase behavior and CO 2 infinite dilution activity coefficients.

title: Enantioselective Total Syntheses of Bousigonine A and Bisleuconothine B
abstract: Herein, we report the first enantioselective total syntheses of bousigonine A and bisleuconothine B, two heterodimeric monoterpenoid indole alkaloids. The requisite quebrachamine-type and aspidosperma-type alkaloid units were prepared divergently from a common intermediate and subsequently coupled with an eburnan-type alkaloid through bioinspired coupling reactions. The benzyl protecting group on the nitrogen played a crucial role in controlling the regioselectivity of these reactions, enabling selective bond formation at C10.

title: A RecBCD-like enzyme regulates expression of bacterial defense operons in response to DNA damage
abstract: Bacteria must quickly respond to stress signals including bacteriophage (phage) infection, invasion by mobile genetic elements, and other threats. DNA damage is a stress-signaling nexus in bacteria, initiating global responses such as the SOS response and triggering expression of specific defense and immune pathways through DNA damage-sensing transcriptional regulators. Here we identify a three-protein pathway termed Cerberus that senses dsDNA ends that become available during DNA damage or inhibition of the key DNA repair complex RecBCD, and controls expression of an associated defense/immune operon. The central player in Cerberus is a large peptidase-helicase-nuclease fusion protein, CerC, that is architecturally similar to the RecBC complex itself. Upon DNA damage or RecBCD inhibition, CerC binds and unwinds free DNA ends to allosterically activate its fused HExxH metallopeptidase domain. CerC specifically cleaves the adjacently encoded anti-sigma factor CerB to release its cognate sigma factor CerA, allowing CerA to mediate transcription of a defense/immune operon encoded nearby. Cerberus therefore represents a pathway that has co-opted a key DNA repair machine for DNA damage sensing, and linked that activity to transcriptional control through anti-sigma factor cleavage.

title: Uncovering the Multifaceted Role of the Kinetochore Scaffold 1 (KNL1) in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis and CRISPR-Cas9 Experimental Study
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by pronounced heterogeneity, chromosomal instability, and limited therapeutic options. Kinetochore scaffold 1 (KNL1), a core mitotic checkpoint component, is implicated in multiple cancers, but its role in HCC remains unclear. Here, we integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses with functional in vitro validation to elucidate the biological and clinical significance of KNL1 in HCC.

title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental evidence implicate DVL3-associated Wnt/β-catenin signaling in PFHxS-related colorectal cancer progression
abstract: Perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) widely detected in human biospecimens, yet its relationship with colorectal cancer (CRC) progression remains poorly defined. We integrated network toxicology, bulk transcriptomics, machine-learning-based prognostic modeling, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and functional experiments to characterize PFHxS-associated molecular features in CRC.

title: Quantitative imaging of native tissue architecture combined with deep multi-omics reveals the spatial biology of kidney aging
abstract: Aging alters tissue architecture and metabolism in spatially heterogeneous ways, yet the connections between these measurable structural and compositional phenotypes and underlying molecular changes are largely unknown. Here, we introduce NORIGAMI (NoRI-Guided AI for Multimodal Integration), a pipeline combining Normalized Raman Imaging (NoRI), deep learning, quantitative morphology, deep proteomics, and metabolomics to investigate renal aging.

title: Airco opens production site for CO2-to-fuels modules
abstract: E-fuels start-up plans to deliver its first commercial unit to the US military next year

title: How much data does a memory kernel need? Measurement requirements for fractional models of battery and corrosion degradation
abstract: How much data does a memory kernel need before a fit is meaningful? For a distributed-order model, the answer is about 3.1 decades of observation, more than standard battery-degradation tests provide. Battery capacity fade and corrosion-film growth depend on their history, so they are often modelled using general fractional calculus (GFC), where memory is described by an arbitrary Sonine kernel rather than a single power law. We tested this using two mechanistic models without fractional operators and de Levie's porous-electrode model, whose high-frequency order is exactly 0.5; our estimator recovered 0.500. A single aging curve can recover an effective order, alpha, to within 5% noise using a weak formulation, while separating the tempered parameters (alpha, lambda) requires several Arrhenius conditions, with errors improving from (0.25, 0.43) with one condition to (0.04, 0.07) with four. A distributed-order memory needs 3.1 decades of data to be resolved to 90%; below that, a two-order memory can collapse into one intermediate order that fits the data better than the true spectrum. For saturating passivation, however, a general kernel improves the fit substantially, raising R2 from 0.862 to 0.998. Across 20 cells from two public datasets, observation windows span only 1.23 to 2.24 decades, making the 3.1-decade result a practical design rule: it defines what must be measured before fitting a memory kernel, not only what cannot be fitted.

title: End-to-end reconstruction for cryo electron ptychographic single-particle analysis
abstract: Cryo-electron ptychographic (cryo-ptycho) single-particle analysis (SPA) is a diffractive imaging method for protein structure determination. Current reconstruction workflows sequentially reconstruct a 2D phase micrograph from each scan, and then apply conventional SPA software to the resulting projections to obtain a 3D potential map. Here, we introduce End2EndPtychoSPA, an end-to-end reconstruction algorithm that directly fits a 3D electrostatic potential volume and particle poses to 4D-STEM diffraction data using a differentiable multislice forward model. On simulated haemoglobin data where the sequential route recovers initial poses, End2EndPtychoSPA with a learnable vitreous-ice layer reaches 3.22 A resolution against the ground truth (FSC 0.5), compared with 3.41 A for the sequential route. We also compare End2EndPtychoSPA with the sequential route on four published experimental cryo-ptycho SPA datasets. On apoferritin (11,552 particles), the End2EndPtychoSPA map improves agreement with an external atomic model over both our matched sequential route on the same particles and the deposited EMD-19425 half-map mean, and shifts the unmasked half-map FSC 0.143 crossing from 6.83 A to 5.99 A. On T20S, TMV and Phi92, End2EndPtychoSPA does not yet improve upon the 2D route.

title: MASH-in-a-dish reveals fatty acid-driven itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is characterized by lipid-driven sterile inflammation and fibrosis that leads to liver failure and liver cancer. Metabolites are increasingly recognized as signaling molecules and regulate disease progression through cell-cell crosstalk. To overcome the challenges of studying metabolite crosstalk between different cell types in MASH livers, we developed a novel in vitro MASH model, "MASH-in-a-dish", a Transwell co-culture system of mouse hepatocyte-derived organoids (HepOrgs), Kupffer cells (KCs), and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) in a…

title: Molecular crowding differentially regulates magnetic field-dependent fluorescence, recovery kinetics, and photostability of the magnetosensitive protein MagLOV2
abstract: Macromolecular crowding and solvent composition can alter protein conformation, diffusion, hydration, and cofactor photophysics, yet their influence on magnetically sensitive flavoproteins is poorly understood. We tested seven molecular environments in MagLOV2-overexpressing Escherichia coli lysate using a custom-built, high-intensity magnetofluorescence platform. Five-point concentration series of Dextran 70, Ficoll PM70, PEG6000, PEG3350, glycerol, ethylene glycol, and bovine serum albumin (BSA) were measured at 22 mT under continuous 6.12 W/cm2 blue-light excitation. Dextran 70, Ficoll PM70, and PEG6000 progressively attenuated the negative magnetic field effect (MFE), whereas PEG3350 shifted toward mild enhancement at higher concentrations. Glycerol and ethylene glycol enhanced the negative MFE despite producing the strongest slowing of recovery upon the field being switched off (OFF-recovery), while BSA modestly enhanced MFE and accelerated OFF-recovery. Across 105 treatment cuvettes, the change in MFE was not globally correlated with changes in the OFF-recovery time constant (r = -0.07, p = 0.449). The initial pre-field illumination period revealed a second phenotype: Dextran and Ficoll increased late fluorescence loss, whereas glycerol and BSA were photoprotective. Pre-field fluorescence loss correlated moderately with MFE change across the full dataset (r = 0.474, p = 3.28 x 10-7) but not consistently within crowder classes. These findings show that MagLOV2 spin-dependent magnetofluorescence is shaped by crowder chemistry, polymer size, solvent environment, recovery kinetics, and photostability rather than by a single generic crowding or viscosity mechanism.

title: Role of Intermolecular Association in Monolayer-Level Assembly and Morphogenesis of Conjugated Polymers at the Air–Water Interface
abstract: How molecular architecture is translated through intermolecular association into film structure and mechanical behavior remains a central question in conjugated-polymer self-assembly. Here, we compare two luminescent polymers with distinct backbone and side-chain structures: poly(9,9-di-n-octylfluorenyl-2,7-diyl) (PFO) and poly(2,5-di(3′,7′-dimethyloctyl)phenylene-1,4-ethynylene) (PPE).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Computational Quantum Chemistry-Based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction Framework: Application in Sulfate Aerosol Formation Mechanisms
abstract: Atmospheric isotope serves as an effective source tracer for tracking the pollutants fate. Its precise source apportionment capability is constrained by the comprehensive assessment of isotope fractionation. This study aimed to propose a Computational Quantum Chemistry (CQC)-based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction (AIFP) framework. It can quantify the isotope fractionation mechanisms. This framework utilizes CQC to perform a pipeline for reaction mechanism determination, atmospheric species geometry calculation, and parameter post-processing.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
