title: The weight of memory: nutrition, diabetes, and the brain
abstract: This issue of the Biomedical Journal explores therapeutic approaches to neuroinflammation, antimicrobial resistance, and cancer, as well as developments in laboratory testing and prognostic assessment. Experimental findings show that glibenclamide attenuates palmitic acid-induced hippocampal inflammation and memory impairment in mice. In antimicrobial research, CRISPR-Cas9-mediated elimination of resistance genes restores ertapenem susceptibility in resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, while deep learning offers an approach to interpreting antimicrobial susceptibility tests from images.

title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
abstract: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.

title: A Biodegradable Metal–Organic Framework/Oligomer Composite for Sustainable Gold Recovery and Circular Water Management
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is generating unprecedented e-waste streams rich in secondary gold resources, yet sustainable recovery strategies remain scarce. Here, we report a bioderived, environmentally degradable metal–organic framework (MOF)/oligomer composite (SU-102/pGSH) constructed via host–guest self-assembly of glutathione (GSH) within a Zr-ellagate framework.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists
abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. However, the structural complexity and conformational plasticity of class B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) make conventional single-method virtual screening approaches prone to bias and limited chemotype recovery. Using an integrated ligand- and structure-based virtual screening pipeline, combining complementary ligand-based descriptors, multifingerprint similarity, electrostatic similarity, pharmacophore modeling, and multiconformation docking under a consensus-driven selection strategy, we identified three chemically distinct GLP-1R agonists comprising one nonpeptidic molecule (GQB47810), and two peptides (neuromedin C and DPDPE). Among them, DPDPE showed the greatest effectiveness, reaching nearly 100% of the maximal GLP-1 response, although with lower potency (EC50 = 4.3 μM). Further in vitro characterization confirmed that DPDPE behaved as a full agonist and exhibited dual agonistic activity at GLP-1R and at the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR, EC50 = 4.3 μM). Site-directed mutagenesis of the predicted binding site, with cell-surface expression measured for every mutant, and whole-cell competition binding against 125I-GLP-1 are consistent with direct engagement of the receptor. These findings establish a consensus-driven computational framework for chemotype-diverse agonist discovery at conformationally flexible GPCR targets and reveal a pentapeptide with GLP-1-like efficacy as a promising lead for next-generation small peptide therapeutics.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Conductive Composite-Based Wearable Sensors for Sports Science: Intelligent Data Analysis and Emerging Applications
abstract: Wearable sensors enable continuous acquisition of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals during exercise, providing data to support sports performance assessment, training regulation, fatigue monitoring, and rehabilitation interventions. However, signal reliability and multidimensional data analysis under complex motion conditions remain constrained by device functionality.

title: A combined segmented anode gas ionization chamber and time-of-flight detector for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis
abstract: A dedicated detector system for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis at the Tandem Laboratory of Uppsala University is presented. Benefits of combining a time-of-flight measurement with a segmented anode gas ionization chamber are demonstrated. The capability of ion species identification is improved with the present system, compared to that obtained when using a single solid state silicon detector for the full ion energy signal. The system enables separation of light elements, up to Neon, based on atomic number while signals from heavy elements such as molybdenum and tungsten are separated based on mass, to a sample depth on the order of one micrometer. The performance of the system is discussed and a selection of material analysis applications is given. Plasma-facing materials from fusion experiments, in particular metal mirrors, are used as a main example for the discussion. Marker experiments using nitrogen-15 or oxygen-18 are specific cases for which the described improved species separation and sensitivity are required. Resilience to radiation damage and significantly improved energy resolution for heavy elements at low energies are additional benefits of the gas ionization chamber over a solid state detector based system.

title: Intraoperative Tumor-Tissue Discrimination and Histology-Defined Glioma Grading Using Combined Fluorescence and Diffuse Reflectance Spectroscopy
abstract: BackgroundMaximal safe glioma resection requires distinguishing infiltrative tumor from surrounding brain. Visible 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA)-induced protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) fluorescence guides surgery, but low or heterogeneous PpIX accumulation and optical attenuation limit sensitivity. We tested whether combined fluorescence spectroscopy (FS) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) could improve tumor-tissue discrimination beyond visible fluorescence.MethodsThirty-three patients with historically classified low-grade (LGG), high-grade (HGG), or recurrent glioma underwent 5-ALA-guided…

title: Tumor-cell TOP2A contributes to ochratoxin A-enhanced hepatocellular carcinoma progression and impaired CD8⁺ T-cell responses
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) is a widespread foodborne mycotoxin with hepatotoxic and immunotoxic effects, but its role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and antitumor immunity remains unclear. Here, we integrated network toxicology, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, molecular interaction assays, and experimental validation to identify key molecular factors associated with OTA-enhanced HCC progression.

title: Clozapine and Metabolic Syndrome: Evidence from Integrative Bioinformatics and Molecular Simulation
abstract: Clozapine is an effective treatment for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but its clinical use is limited by the high risk of developing metabolic syndrome (MetS). This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets and biological mechanisms underlying clozapine-induced MetS. We integrated clozapine-related targets, MetS‑related genes, and differentially expressed genes from the GSE98895 dataset to identify candidate targets.

title: Topology-Directed Pore Space Compartmentalization and Densification in MOFs Enable Record Trace C3H6 Capture and C2H4 Purification
abstract: Adsorptive separation of C3H6 from C2H4 is of great relevance yet highly challenging to the petrochemical industry, especially for trace C3H6 capture. Here, we constructed two metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), NKU-410 and NKU-411, through pillaring of the kgd- and hxl-topology supermolecular building layers (SBLs) comprised of a novel fluoride-bridging hexanuclear niccolite cluster.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Altering the E. coli Ribosome Exit Tunnel to Improve Consecutive Incorporation of Challenging Monomers
abstract: Ribosomes are capable of incorporating a wide array of natural and unnatural monomers into growing polymer chains, but can be stalled by monomers with constrained or non-natural backbones. Here we evaluate whether monomer-dependent ribosome stalling can be alleviated by structure-guided mutations to 23S rRNA within the exit tunnel. Escherichia coli (E. coli) ribosomes harboring an A2062U mutation are as active as wild type (WT) ribosomes when translating nonproline sequences and up to 10-fold more active when translating sequences containing three or four consecutive proline residues. High-resolution cryo-EM structures of WT and A2062U mutant ribosomes containing a polyproline nascent chain reveal that the A2062U mutation relieves an exit tunnel constriction to better accommodate a conformationally restricted peptide chain. A2062U mutant ribosomes also improve translation of sequences containing multiple, consecutive β2-hydroxy acids. These results provide a mechanistic basis for engineering the E. coli ribosome for improved translation of genetically encoded polymers with novel backbones.

title: Ultrashort laser pulses can slice lab-grown diamond along useful crystal plane
abstract: More than just a precious gemstone for jewelry, diamond has properties that make it attractive for several next-generation, high-performance technologies. Its high thermal conductivity can help move heat away from semiconductor devices, while its wide bandgap is promising for high-power electronics. Moreover, its transparency in the visible light range makes diamond useful for demanding optical applications.

title: Computational identification of EBNA1-binding candidates using machine learning-based virtual screening and molecular docking.
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is associated with several malignancies and multiple sclerosis, and Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) plays an essential role in viral genome replication and episome maintenance. The experimentally characterized KVD-associated pocket within the EBNA1 DNA-binding domain provides a structurally defined site for computational ligand prioritization. This study aimed to identify and prioritize predicted EBNA1-binding candidates using an integrated machine-learning and structure-based virtual screening framework.

title: Chemistry-transforming applications of artificial intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used across chemical research, but its practical value depends on where it intervenes in the workflow and how reliably it generalizes beyond curated benchmarks. This review adopts a pipeline-based perspective: we first decompose chemical research into stages that generate, transform, and validate information and then map AI methods onto these stages with an emphasis on measurable outcomes and failure modes.

title: Machine learning-based thermoelectric materials screening with physical consistency and uncertainty propagation
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising strategy for accelerating thermoelectric materials discovery. However, direct prediction of the thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) often can introduce target leakage and overestimates predictive performance because ZT is intrinsically derived from multiple transport properties. In this work, a physics-guided and uncertainty-aware ML framework is developed for thermoelectric material screening by independently predicting the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, and thermal conductivity, followed by analytical evaluation of thermoelectric performance. Experimental data from the ESTM database were evaluated using material-wise validation, with exact chemical formulas kept exclusively in either the training or held-out test subset to reduce material-level information leakage. Predictive uncertainty was quantified using ensemble learning and propagated into thermoelectric performance evaluation and uncertainty-aware LCB screening. The proposed framework demonstrates strong predictive capability for individual transport properties while providing physically consistent thermoelectric performance estimation. Although the framework exhibits lower apparent predictive accuracy than direct ZT regression models, it provides improved interpretability and a more physically structured approach to thermoelectric performance evaluation. The results demonstrate that integrating physical consistency, uncertainty propagation, and uncertainty-aware screening provides a robust strategy for data-driven thermoelectric materials screening.

title: Aligning Molecules and Fragments in a Shared Embedding Space for Property-Aware Fragment Selection
abstract: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. We introduce Molecule–Fragment Representation Alignment for Generation (M-FRAG), a property-aware framework that aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Divergent Reactivity toward Decarboxylative Protonation or Oxidation via Single-Component Organocatalysis
abstract: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.

title: Process-intrinsic cellular network for sustained strength–ductility across temperatures in a 3D-printed multi-principal-element alloy
abstract: Laser-based additive manufacturing enables the formation of a self-assembled precipitate cellular network in a multi-principal element alloy, which sustains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Dietary Management and Nutritional Interventions: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence, Applications, and Translational Challenges
abstract: This narrative review examines the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in nutrition and dietetics, focusing on AI-assisted dietary assessment, precision nutrition, generative AI for dietary counselling, and the ethical, regulatory, and implementation challenges affecting clinical translation. A critical narrative synthesis of evidence on AI applications in nutrition and dietetics was undertaken, covering convolutional neural network (CNN)-based food image recognition and portion estimation, machine learning (ML) models for predicting postprandial glycaemic response (PPGR), and large…
venue: Journal of the American Nutrition Association

title: Artificial neural network and Bvp4c approach for mixed convective magnetized Casson nanoliquid flow and heat transportation over a stretchable cylinder under the presence of activation energy and nth order chemical reaction
abstract: The goal of the current study is to investigate mixed convection magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) heat transfer in non-Newtonian Casson nanoliquid flowing across a stretching cylinder under the collective effects of thermal radiation, activation energy, and nth order chemical reaction. The present proposed model is applicable to industrial processes involving cooling of cylindrical components and high-temperature manufacturing systems. Convective boundary conditions, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, and mixed-convection effects are included in the mathematical model to capture the transport phenomena adequately. The transformed governing differential equations are then solved numerically using hybrid approach bvp4c and ANN. To improve predictive capability and computational efficiency, a Levenberg-Marquardt-based Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is developed using the numerical dataset generated from the bvp4c solutions. The dataset is subdivided into 70% of training, 15% of validation, and 15% of testing, and the ANN predictions exhibit excellent agreement with the numerical results, demonstrating high accuracy and strong generalization performance. The effects of the governing parameters on the velocity, temperature, and concentration distributions are examined comprehensively. The novel results reveal that increasing the magnetic parameter and Casson fluid parameter suppresses the velocity field, whereas thermal radiation and convective heating significantly enhance the temperature distribution. Moreover, higher activation energy intensifies the concentration profile, while enhancing the order of chemical reaction reduces nanoparticle concentration. The variations in wall friction coefficient, local Nusselt number, and local Sherwood number are also quantified and discussed in detail. Comparison with previously published limiting cases confirms the accuracy and reliability of the proposed numerical methodology. The findings demonstrate that the hybrid bvp4c-ANN framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for analyzing complex nonlinear nanofluid transport problems encountered in advanced thermal engineering, energy systems, and industrial heat transfer applications..

title: The small ORF (smORF)-encoded polypeptide MIRINE promotes neuronal differentiation in vertebrate brain development
abstract: The vertebrate brain expresses an extensive repertoire of long-noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), an emerging source of small open reading frame (smORF)-encoded polypeptides (SEPs) whose functions remain largely unknown. Using ribosome profiling and proteomics of zebrafish and mouse brain, we identified hundreds of translated smORFs. We characterized MIRINE, a SEP of 83 amino acids conserved across 205 vertebrate species. MIRINE contains a transmembrane domain that targets it to the plasma membrane and intracellular vesicles, and is enriched in cortical and hippocampal neurons, with expression rising during neurogenesis. Downregulation of Mirine increased cell proliferation and impaired neuronal maturation in neuroblastoma cells, in mouse primary cortical neurons and cortex, and in the zebrafish forebrain, identifying MIRINE as a regulator of the balance between neuronal proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, MIRINE associates with the synaptic-vesicle protein Synaptogyrin-3 and related membrane proteins. Our findings define a conserved, membrane-associated SEP controlling neuronal maturation and illustrate the functional potential of brain SEPs.

title: Exploring Liquid Metals as Dynamic Reaction Media
abstract: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements.

title: An Integrated Experimental and Informatics Strategy Enables Large Proteoform Identification in Top-Down Proteomics
abstract: Top-down proteomics enables identification and characterization of intact proteoforms, preserving information on co-occurring sequence variations and post-translational modifications. However, identifying large proteoforms remains challenging due to an exponential decrease in signal-to-noise ratio with increasing molecular weight, interference from coeluting smaller species, unresolved precursor isotopic envelopes, difficulty obtaining informative MS/MS spectra, and limitations of current informatics tools.

title: Decoding antibody-antigen recognition: the BL8 language and its application in calibrating deep learning predictions
abstract: Antibodies are central to immunology and therapeutics, and understanding how they recognize antigens is essential to rational drug design. This recognition depends on the interplay of interface geometry, physicochemical interactions, sequence context, and complementarity-determining region (CDR) conformation. However, traditional analyses often oversimplify this complexity, which becomes particularly problematic when evaluating the massive and frequently overconfident structural hypotheses generated by modern deep learning models.

title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit
abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical property analysis, drug-likeness evaluation, structural alert screening, absorption and distribution profiling, CYP450-mediated metabolism prediction, excretion assessment, toxicity evaluation, Tox21 pathway analysis, DrugBank percentile benchmarking, and composite multi-parameter optimisation scoring. A total of 104 ADMET-related outputs were generated per compound, including 52 predictive endpoints and 52 corresponding DrugBank approved-drug percentile rankings. The 200 curated CDK2 inhibitors exhibited 100% Lipinski Ro5 compliance, 38.5% predicted CYP3A4 inhibition, 73.5% predicted hERG liability, and 99.5% predicted DILI risk, with a mean composite ADMET score of 0.46 and a mean traffic light green flag count of 9.5/13. The workflow provides an accessible and FAIR-compliant framework for ADMET analysis, cheminformatics education, and reproducible computational drug discovery.Scientific contributionThis work contributes a structured educational framework for teaching and implementing computational ADMET analysis in modern drug discovery. To be explicit about the nature of this contribution: the novelty is pedagogical and integrative rather than methodological, no new prediction model, algorithm, or endpoint is introduced. The study demonstrates how an existing graph neural network-based prediction model (ADMET-AI) can be integrated with open-source cheminformatics workflows to support interpretable and reproducible pharmacokinetic assessment. Beyond endpoint prediction, the tutorial emphasises practical data handling, workflow automation, compound prioritisation, and transparent result interpretation within a Jupyter notebook environment. The inclusion of DrugBank percentile benchmarking, traffic-light visualisation, and composite scoring strategies provides learners and researchers with practical, worked examples of established multi-parameter decision-making approaches during lead optimisation, rather than new decision frameworks in their own right. By combining methodological clarity with FAIR and reproducible research principles, the workflow serves as a scalable resource for cheminformatics education, computational pharmacology training, and ADMET-guided drug development studies.

title: Deciphering Complex Interfacial Dynamics via Operando Microbalance during Potential-Modulated Alkyne Hydrogenation
abstract: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface.

title: Tumor-Specific Gene Editing Enhances Cancer Immunogenicity through Succinate Metabolism-Mediated MHC-I Reprogramming
abstract: Impaired expression of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) greatly compromises cytotoxic T-cell-mediated anticancer immunotherapy. Existing MHC-I activation strategies are greatly challenged by poor tumor specificity and off-target toxicity. Herein, we report a dual tumor-specific CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system that can precisely knock out succinate dehydrogenase subunit C (Sdhc) to activate the MHC-I pathway via epigenetic and transcriptional regulation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Benchmarking Modular Optimization Strategies for Parameterized Quantum Circuits
abstract: Training parameterized quantum circuits requires balancing optimization progress with limited evaluation budgets and the statistical uncertainty of near-term quantum hardware. We present a modular benchmarking framework that separates quantum search-direction estimation from classical parameter-update rules, allowing their interactions and sensitivities to be examined independently.

title: ‘Bonus science’ finds the composition of ultrafine dust on Mars
abstract: The tiny particles may pose a health risk to future astronauts exploring the Red Planet

title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review
abstract: To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026.
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

title: Selective binders of a cotranslational folding intermediate
abstract: Drug discovery efforts typically target mature, folded proteins, primarily to inhibit their function or induce their degradation. An alternative strategy would be to target incompletely folded states that are transiently populated during protein biogenesis, but whether these states contain druggable pockets was unclear. Here, we used an mRNA display approach to discover cyclic peptides that recognize a nascent polypeptide at an intermediate point during its synthesis on the ribosome. We identified peptides that bind with low-nanomolar affinity to a model nascent protein, {beta}-galactosidase, but do not detectably bind either the fully-folded protein or ribosomes synthesising different sequences. Hydrogen/deuterium exchange-mass spectrometry and cryogenic electron microscopy revealed the molecular basis for selective binding. We found that the nascent chain folds into an -helix against the ribosome surface during ongoing translation, creating a cryptic pocket together with ribosomal proteins uL23 and uL29 that is exploited by the hit peptides. Our results establish proof-of-concept for selective targeting of protein biogenesis intermediates, and provide a platform for future drug development.

title: Assessing reinforcement learning and vigor with an online decision-making battery
abstract: Reinforcement learning and vigor are two fundamental aspects of decision-making modulated by dopamine. Although vigor is highly relevant for mood disorders, it has been overlooked by previous batteries characterizing decision-making abilities. We developed a test battery with two RL tasks (RL/working memory, go/no-go task) and two vigor tasks (physical effort discounting, foraging task) and administered it to an online community sample (N = 162). We used computational modeling and factor analysis to identify two factors reflecting RL and vigor. The RL factor reflected participants' general decision-making ability, while vigor corresponded to a motivational propensity to obtain rewards. Both factors demonstrated moderately strong test-retest reliability (ICC(2,1) = .65 and .67, respectively) over a one-to-two-week interval. Moreover, both factors were meaningfully related to self-report scales. The RL and vigor factors were negatively and positively associated with mania, respectively, although further analyses revealed that vigor was not fully independent of RL. Neither factor was significantly associated with depression symptoms. Collectively, we present preliminary evidence that vigor may represent a separate factor from RL in line with the putative dopamine hypothesis, paving the way for future longitudinal assessments of RL and vigor in mood disorders.

title: Single Molecule Diffusion Studies Reveal Rapid Translations Across Target Membrane Surfaces for both p40Phox PX domain and Class III PI3K VPS34 Complex 1, the Autophagy Lipid Kinase
abstract: Single molecule analyses are providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms by which peripheral membrane proteins approach and translate across a target bilayer surface before stable docking. Here we compare and contrast the translational movements of four diffusers on a representative supported lipid bilayer: (i) the fluorescent lipid LRB-(DO)PE, (ii) the G-protein Rab1A anchored to (DO)PE; (iii) the PI(3)P sensor p40Phox PX domain, and (iv) the autophagy lipid kinase VPS34 Complex 1.

title: Recognition of the centromere-binding protein Ndc10 by Scm3HJURP directs Cse4CENP-A deposition at native centromeres
abstract: Kinetochores connect centromeres to spindle microtubules, ensuring accurate chromosome segregation. Kinetochore assembly at centromeres depends on deposition of CENP-A, a histone H3 variant. Despite considerable progress, how CENP-A is specifically assembled on native centromeres remains an open question. Centromere-specific assembly of CENP-A occurs spontaneously in a cell-free extract system from the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, but with low efficiency, suggesting that one or more factors are limiting. Here, we show Scm3HJURP, a specific chaperone for the centromeric histone Cse4CENP-A, is one such limiting component. The addition of a complex of Scm3, Cse4 and histone H4 strongly stimulates Cse4 assembly in a centromeric DNA sequence- and dose-dependent manner; in addition, improvements in both Cse4 and kinetochore assembly were more prominent in mitotic versus interphase (G1) extracts. Using the complemented cell-free reconstitution system, we show that distinct Scm3 interfaces with Cse4 and with the Ndc10 subunit of the yeast centromere DNA sequence-recognizing CBF3 complex are essential for centromere-specific Cse4 assembly and cell viability. Thus, recognition of Ndc10 directs Scm3-dependent and locus-specific centromeric histone deposition.

title: Heterogeneous primary nucleation determines Aβ42 fibrilstructure.
abstract: The current developments in the field of amyloid fibril structure determination has revealed multiple structures for peptides of identical sequence. This may reflect variations in sample environment or similar nucleation barriers for multiple folds. Here we investigate the influence of aggregating surface and during fibril formation from monomeric amyloid {beta} peptide (A{beta}42). The fibril structures formed in identical solutions in glass vials / bottles and PEGylated polystyrene 96-well plates display very different monomer fold within the fibrils.

title: Hydroxyl-Directed Anchoring and Electronic Structure of Pt–Sn on γ-Al2O3 for Propane Dehydrogenation
abstract: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3.

title: Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
abstract: Non-resonant excitation of WS2 in-plane microcavities generates waveguide exciton–polaritons that carry spin-polarized currents over distances exceeding 90 μm at room temperature and reveal a non-resonantly pumped optical spin Hall effect.

title: Excited-State Branching in Optovin: Resolving the Photophysics of a Gene-Free Optopharmacological Tool
abstract: Optovin is a small, light-activated molecule that enables optical control of TRPA1 ion channels without genetic modification, making it a landmark tool in optopharmacology. However, the excited-state pathways initiated by photoexcitation, and how these may relate to optovin function, have remained unresolved. Here, we show that optovin’s photophysics in solution are governed by competition between rapid photoisomerization and intersystem crossing. Violet-light excitation prepares the bright S2(ππ*) state, which rapidly relaxes over picoseconds to the dark S1(nπ*) state. Most excited molecules subsequently decay through torsional Z-E photoisomerization over tens of picoseconds, providing a reversible nonradiative pathway. In parallel, a minor fraction (10–30% depending on solvent) of the excited-state population undergoes intersystem crossing to form a short-lived triplet state that persists for up to a nanosecond. Direct near-infrared detection of singlet oxygen confirms triplet-mediated oxygen sensitization, although with a low apparent quantum yield of a fraction of a percent, with no dependence on the initial isomeric composition of optovin. These results identify competition between torsional internal conversion and intersystem crossing as the central branching process in optovin photophysics. These intrinsic excited-state dynamics provide experimentally defined constraints on models of TRPA1 activation and establish photophysical design principles for next-generation, gene-free optopharmacological agents.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
abstract: Artificial intelligence has accelerated the design of structured proteins, but it remains difficult to design functional intrinsically disordered proteins because of weak structural constraints and poorly defined sequence-to-function relationships1. Activation domains (ADs), transcription factor regions that recruit coactivators, are an excellent test case for the de novo design of intrinsically disordered sequences. ADs are one of the oldest groups of functional intrinsically disordered sequences2 and designed ADs have applications in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and agriculture. We computationally generated 500,000 candidate sequences that resembled known ADs and predicted AD function with extant machine learning models, including three neural networks. From high-scoring sequences, we selected 18,750 for experimental validation in yeast. Surprisingly, >90% of the 16,770 well-measured sequences function as ADs. Sequences predicted to be active by multiple models were stronger, motivating development of a fast and accurate consensus AD predictor, MADRIGAL. A number of our designed ADs retain functionality across fungi, plants, and human cells. This work illustrates a generalizable paradigm for incorporating sequence-to-function models into the design loop to efficiently generate functional intrinsically disordered sequences.

title: ToxINsight: An Integrated Web Platform for Sequence, Structure, and Ligand Binding Analysis of Snake Venom Toxins
abstract: Around 5.4 million people worldwide are bitten by snakes each year, with 1.8 to 2.7 million cases of envenomation, of which 81,410 to 137,880 people die from snake envenomation worldwide each year. It is categorized as a high-priority Category A Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD) by the World Health Organization (WHO). A molecular level understanding of snake venom toxins and their mechanisms of action is crucial for development of efficient therapeutics tackling snake envenomation.

title: Inferring scaling laws of branching networks from their geometry by global optimization
abstract: Optimality principles are widely used to understand branching networks, yet they are tested on individual branchings that cannot reliably distinguish competing scaling laws. We formulate the missing link between the laws and measurements by mapping each law to its predicted branch points through global optimization. Vascular branch points closely match weighted-length optima when each vessel is allowed its own fitted weight. Inferred scaling laws reveal type-specific geometric signatures hidden from local analysis.

title: Ultra-precision 3D Printed Sample Tubes of Complex Cross Section for Enhanced Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Sensitivity of AqueousSamples
abstract: This paper discusses the applications of ultra-precision 3D printing in developing EPR sample tubes for X-band measurements of aqueous samples. The seed idea of this work started from the flat cell idea discussed in Mett and Hyde et al.(2003), Sidabras et al. (2005), and Sidabras et al. (2017), where placing multiple aqueous flat cells perpendicular to the electric field in the microwave cavity reduce RF losses and improve EPR signal sensitivity. In this work, we present the 3D printed aquastar sample holders for dielectric resonators and the aquasun sample holders for cavity resonators. Even though the ultra-precision 3D printing enables the fabrication of complex cross-sections at 25um resolution, the photopolymer material has comparatively higher dielectric losses compared to the conventional materials like glass and PTFE. To reduce the RF losses due to the inherent dielectric properties, we introduced the latticing approach in reducing the amount of plastic without compromising the structural stability. In addition to this, we present the slicing and dielectric approximation approach in reducing the computation cost for these complex cross-sections. The novel sample tubes discussed here present signal improvements through both simulation and experiments, which were validated through power saturation experiments. The sample tube development methodology presented here provide a general framework for designing and implementing 3D printed EPR sample holders, based on resonator electromagnetic field distribution and dielectric properties of the photopolymer material.

title: Filament assembly confers the mechanical resilience of the IFI16 restrictosome
abstract: Interferon-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) is a mammalian innate immune sensor composed of a filament-forming pyrin domain (PYD) followed by tandem HIN200 domains that bind nucleic acids. First recognized as a major regulator of inflammatory responses against cytosolic double-stranded (ds)DNA, IFI16 filaments have been implicated in several key mechanical processes involving both host and pathogens, including viral replication restriction, latency regulation, replication-stress responses, and DNA-damage responses. Moreover, IFI16 filaments are ultra-stable, a key trait believed to drive its autoantigenicity. Although recent studies reported that IFI16 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) via disordered linkers and multivalent protein-dsDNA interactions, whether such a metastable entity provides a framework for the mechanical activities of IFI16 remains unknown. Here, we show that PYD-driven filament assembly confers the mechanical stability of IFI16 condensates by compacting DNA into ultra-stable tangles capable of withstanding forces sufficient to induce duplex deformation. By contrast, HIN200-dsDNA complexes are much more sensitive to ionic perturbation, DNA pretension, and mechanical interference. Together, we demonstrate that filament assembly allows IFI16 to act as a mechano-sensitive restrictor.

title: Spatial Coupling of Metal and Acid Sites via Amorphous Nb–O–Al Interfaces for Selective Polyolefin Hydrocracking
abstract: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking.

title: Functionalization and optimization of biopolymer encapsulants for controlled release in food systems
abstract: The growing interest in biopolymer encapsulants offers a sustainable alternative to synthetic packaging, addressing concerns over plastic pollution and microplastic-related health risks while improving bioactive compound stability. However, poor moisture barrier properties, low mechanical strength, and high production costs hinder their large-scale applications. To address these challenges, chemical and physical functionalization techiques have been developed to enhance material performance, encapsulation efficiency, and the overall functionality of core materials in food applications.

title: Attribution Fingerprinting by Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Category-Specific Additive Design Rules for Zinc Anodes
abstract: Electrolyte additives are one of the most direct remedy for interfacial instability in aqueous zinc-ion batteries, yet their development remains empirical. Existing machine-learning (ML) screening strategies presume a single global structure-property relationship shared by all additives. Here, an interpretable ML framework predicts cycle life from molecular descriptors and test conditions, and molecule-specific SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) profiles serve as attribution fingerprints.

title: Investigating the Toxicological Effects of 3-Phenoxybenzoic Acid Exposure on Sarcopenia via Integrated Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, and In Vitro Validation
abstract: 3-Phenoxybenzoic acid (3-PBA), a widespread degradation product of pyrethroid insecticides, poses potential health risks, but its mechanistic role in sarcopenia remains unclear. We integrated network toxicology, machine learning using LASSO, Elastic Net, random forest, and SVM-RFE, SHAP analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro validation to investigate its underlying effects. A total of 119 candidate genes were prioritized, and five candidate hub genes (GOT2, HDAC4, NDUFS3, ORAI1, and PLIN3) were identified.

title: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
abstract: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

title: Allen--Cahn Residual-Constrained Topology Optimization via an Augmented Lagrangian Method
abstract: This paper presents a residual-constrained topology optimization framework that controls interface transition bandwidth without requiring external density filters. The steady conserved Allen--Cahn (AC) equation is formulated as an equality residual constraint and solved via a mass-weighted Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM) coupled with the Method of Moving Asymptotes (MMA). A closed-form chemical potential projection eliminates the constant residual mode, ensuring algebraic compatibility with external volume targets. Variational sensitivity analysis reveals a symmetric-plus-rank-one Jacobian that yields matrix-free sensitivities without additional adjoint PDE solves, reducing residual sensitivity overhead to only 0.11% of the state elasticity solve time in 3D. Systematic 2D benchmarks confirm that interface bandwidth is governed intrinsically by reaction--diffusion parameters across mesh refinements. While diffuse interfaces incur a continuous compliance elevation (1.4%--12.3%), a volume-preserving 0/1 post-processing audit across 48 benchmark cases demonstrates that this gap stems primarily from intermediate-density penalization: binarized AC-ALM designs achieve equal or superior stiffness in 45 configurations (averaging 1.2% stiffer than SIMP). Simultaneously, single-node hinges and strut fragmentation are substantially suppressed compared to unregularized baselines. Three-dimensional benchmarks further demonstrate practical spatial viability for complex structures.

title: Embedding a de Rham Complex Structure into Eig-PIELM for Maxwell Eigenvalue Problems
abstract: The perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary condition alone does not eliminate the gradient nullspace of the Maxwell curl-curl operator. Consequently, a boundary-only Maxwell implementation of Eig-PIELM, an eigenvalue extension of the physics-informed extreme learning machine (PIELM), may retain represented gradient modes in its reduced trial space, producing nonphysical, gradient-contaminated modes. We develop dR-Eig-PIELM, a finite-dimensional structure-preserving extension that retains the linear-coefficient, boundary-null-space, and one-shot multimode architecture of Eig-PIELM. It combines compatible tensor-product grad--curl trial spaces with a constrained null-space construction to restrict the sampled PEC space to the mass-orthogonal complement of the represented gradient image before the eigensolve. Symmetric weak-form Gram assembly yields a symmetric-definite reduced eigenproblem without an eigenvalue cutoff under the stated sampling and material-positivity assumptions. For rectangles and cuboids, we establish fixed-degree exactness at the PEC vector-field space and derive rank and dimension identities. Numerical experiments show that dR-Eig-PIELM excludes the spurious eigenmodes with significant gradient components observed in the boundary-only baseline. The method exhibits rapid convergence with increasing polynomial degree and competitive work--precision performance in the tested configurations. A covariantly mapped waveguide example illustrates the potential of dR-Eig-PIELM for integration into design optimization workflows through a constrained local geometry update driven by computed cutoff frequencies and their sensitivities. This work provides a mathematical and computational framework for separating represented gradient modes from physical Maxwell eigenmodes within Eig-PIELM and supports its use in waveguide spectral analysis and geometry design.

title: GPU infrastructure for ML/MM with electrostatic embedding for enzyme chemistry
abstract: We present a fully GPU-native framework for machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) enhanced sampling simulations with electrostatic embedding, demonstrated on an enzymatic reaction. The framework combines a JAX port of the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model, an electrostatic embedding scheme compatible with the MACE-POLAR architecture, and integration with JAX-MD and PLUMED-JAX for end-to-end compiled enhanced sampling. The implementation is developed using GPT-6.1-Sol within Codex, with reasoning effort set to high. Using replica exchange umbrella sampling, we calculate the free energy profile of nucleophilic substitution in haloalkane dehalogenase in approximately 200 H100 GPU hours, treating the entire protein and reactants with MACE-POLAR-1-M-JAX and most of the solvent with molecular mechanics.

title: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
abstract: HfO$_2$ heterostructures with La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO$_2$ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO$_2$, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO$_2$ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ and ZrO$_2$ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO$_2$-based materials.

title: The effect of local stacking fault fluctuations on dislocation glide and the interplay with solid solution strengthening in Al-Mg alloys
abstract: Concentrated alloys are characterized by a random arrangement of solute atoms of different sizes, which generates spatially fluctuating displacement and stress fields with non-trivial correlations. This chemical disorder also induces local fluctuations in stacking-fault (SF) energies, giving rise to fluctuating SF forces acting on the partial dislocations bounding the SF. In this work, we investigate the characteristics of the SF noise, including spatial correlations and the impact of such SF energy fluctuations on dislocation glide. Specifically, the gliding behavior of screw, edge, and mixed dislocations in a model concentrated Al-Mg random alloy with varying Mg content is analyzed. The interplay between SF energy fluctuations and solid-solution noise is also discussed. We show that SF forces are spatially correlated, in close analogy with long-range elastic stresses, and exhibit a robust negative correlation along the slip direction. We identify the physical origin of these correlations and demonstrate that they significantly contribute to the critical resolved shear stress for dislocations to glide. In contrast, correlations in other directions are weaker but can still be non-negligible, depending on the underlying interatomic interactions.

title: A new way to make better use of ruthenium in single-atom catalysts
abstract: Ruthenium (Ru) is a valuable metal used in catalysts to speed up chemical reactions in many industrial processes. It can help improve efficiency and reduce the energy needed for chemical production. However, because it is rare and expensive, scientists are looking for ways to make better use of it.

title: Multiplicity of elastic wave propagation in random polycrystals
abstract: The coherent elastic wave in untextured polycrystals, central to ultrasonic and seismic characterization, was recently observed to have two modes per polarization at short wavelengths. However, their physical origin and amplitude partition have remained open. We address both by theory, grain-scale numerical simulations and a grain velocity estimate. The first-order smoothing approximation, simplified by the far-field approximation, predicts three waves, which are the classical effective wave and one for each type of scattered wave (longitudinal and transverse). At long wavelengths, only the effective wave is weakly attenuated. At short wavelengths, one of the other two waves joins it with comparable attenuation, whereas the third stays far more attenuated. A new residue method, which needs no fitting, gives the same pattern for the amplitude partition, with the two waves sharing the coherent field and the third carrying little. The simulations reveal exactly these two modes, for transverse waves in iron and longitudinal waves in strongly anisotropic SrMgSn, and never the third. The wavefields reveal the mechanism, in which the incident wave is extinguished within one grain correlation length and the coherent field is rebuilt by forward multiple scattering. Strikingly, a grain velocity estimate from single-crystal constants provides independent evidence, tracing the two modes to plane waves of the individual grains and closely reproducing their velocities. Observability of multiple waves is thus set by attenuation and amplitude partition together, and short-wavelength measurements in random media must allow for more than one coherent mode.

title: Exploit or conform? How norm utility prompting changes the way LLMs use community beliefs
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) serve both as tools for aiding human decision-making in everyday life and as models of human agents in experimental simulation studies. Alignment on prototypical social decisions -- such as whether to cooperate on a collective action -- therefore has immediate practical consequences for researchers and for society at large. Here we systematically explore the impact of ``norm utility'' -- the non-material components of utility that account for an individual's desire to conform to social norms and to be internally consistent -- on the strategic decision-making of three open-weight LLMs in one-shot, two-player social dilemmas. We find that when a social dilemma is presented together with information about community beliefs -- but without any indication of how those beliefs should matter -- models tend to treat community belief as strategic information, so that in the Snowdrift game cooperation falls as community belief in cooperation increases. When we explicitly prompt the components of norm utility this relationship inverts, and cooperation increases with community belief, in broad agreement with the predictions of a simple norm utility model. We then show that prompting norm utility reduces the volatility of strategic decisions with respect to changes in the underlying social context, and generates more consistent reasoning habits across models. Taken together, our results suggest that prompting norm utility can help generate more human-like and consistent behavior across models and lower volatility within models.

title: TB-Transolver: Parallelized and Coherent Long-Horizon Rollouts via Temporal Bundling for Time-Dependent PDEs
abstract: Transolver has recently gained widespread adoption for solving diverse physical problems on unstructured geometric meshes by leveraging its Physics-Attention mechanism, which seamlessly extends standard softmax attention to handle physical domains at scale. For time-dependent problems, existing literature relies on time-conditioned or autoregressive rollouts to preserve temporal causality while retaining Physics-Attention as the spatial backbone. However, a fundamental limitation of this formulation is its sequential execution model, wherein computational costs scale linearly with the temporal horizon, rendering standard Transolver inefficient for transient problems despite its exceptional spatial efficacy. This bottleneck has historically hindered its broader application in time-dependent physical modeling. To address this limitation, we introduce TB-Transolver (also referred to as Temporally Bundled Transolver), an efficient framework built on temporal bundling that scales Transolver for time-dependent PDEs. Furthermore, we propose \emph{spatiotemporal coherence} (${\rm C(K)}$) as a general metric to systematically quantify snapshot correlation within a temporal bundle, enabling the \emph{a priori} selection of optimal bundle widths using training data alone, thereby avoiding expensive grid searches. We demonstrate the computational efficacy of TB-Transolver across four physically distinct domains, namely, plasticity, fluid dynamics, reaction-diffusion, and global weather forecasting; achieving training speedups of up to $29\times$ over conventional autoregressive and time-conditioned baselines. Finally, these computational gains are further amplified through distributed multi-node and multi-GPU parallelism, yielding aggregated speedups of up to $45.6\times$ at optimal bundle widths for systems exhibiting high spatiotemporal coherence compared to single-GPU implementations.

title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) convert low-frequency mechanical energy into electricity and enable self-powered sensing. Their performance depends on interactions among material properties, surface morphology, contact mechanics, charge generation and external circuits. This review examines these interactions across length scales to assess how material and interface descriptions support predictive device design. Polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials are discussed in relation to charge generation and retention, mechanical compliance, durability and application requirements. Modelling approaches span molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations, rough-surface contact mechanics, device-scale electrostatics and equivalent circuits. Their capabilities are assessed through the inputs they require, the quantities they predict and the experimental evidence used for validation. Particular attention is given to prescribed surface charge density, idealised geometries and nominal contact-area assumptions, which constrain predictions under realistic loading conditions. Applications are organised by macroscale, milliscale and microscale device dimensions to examine requirements for materials, architecture and integration. The review identifies evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay as critical links between interfacial behaviour and electrical output. A staged validation strategy is proposed for contact mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response, with independent testing beyond calibration conditions. These priorities guide the development of multiscale models and reliable TENG systems.

title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
abstract: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and reflections on what to improve. Recursa bootstraps the repository from domain materials and then refines it through recursive self-improvement. It uses parallel learners to execute tasks and synthesize local improvements, then validates and merges the improvements into the knowledge repository. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, Recursa raises the all-pass rate on held-out test tasks from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash.

title: Dynamical Phonon Anharmonicity Drives Charge-Density-Wave Softening and Electronic Quasiparticle Decoherence in Monolayer 1H-NbSe2
abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
abstract: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.

title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?
abstract: Scientific discovery builds on accurate observations interpreted through domain knowledge and reasoning. For scientific 3D data, this requires understanding structures and spatial relationships, from protein contacts to anatomical organization. Existing multimodal benchmarks largely evaluate text and 2D images, while scientific 3D evaluations vary in representations and protocols across disciplines, limiting cross-disciplinary comparison. To assess these foundational capabilities, we introduce ScienceVision, a cross-domain benchmark for scientific 3D understanding and reasoning through expert-level visual question answering (VQA). We construct 250 questions, with 50 each from Biology, Chemistry, Medical Imaging, Mechanical CAD, and Architecture, through a pipeline combining synthetic question generation with domain-expert review and annotation. Each task pairs a native 3D artifact with a scientific question, a specified response format, and a task-specific reference answer, requiring domain knowledge to be applied to geometric or topological evidence. We evaluate 12 models on the same questions in three settings: visual question answering with native 3D artifacts accessed through an agent harness's file and code-execution tools; the same workflow augmented with expert-inspired viewer inspection and measurement tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP); and visual question answering from prescribed rendered 2D images using an agent harness. All settings use the same task-specific deterministic final-answer scoring. The inspection environment supports view changes, target isolation, and slice inspection. In this main comparison, the best mean answer score is 0.53 out of 1. Mean scores in the native-artifact workflow without additional MCP tools exceed those in the rendered-image workflow for every model, by 17.2 percentage points on average.

title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

title: Magnetically and electrically tunable nonlinear Hall effect in Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets
abstract: Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets can exhibit multiferroicity with coexisting ferroelectricity and magnetic order, and thus host multiple order-parameter configurations. However, how to electrically read out these configurations is an issue meriting further investigation. Here, by combining tight-binding and first-principles calculations, we propose electrically and magnetically tunable nonlinear Hall transport in ferroelectric Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets. Model calculations show that ferroelectric switching can reverse the sign of the Berry curvature dipole (BCD), whereas the Neel vector rotation modulates its magnitude, allowing both ferroelectric and magnetic order to be reflected in the nonlinear Hall signal. First-principles calculations of the VOCl2 monolayer confirm these behaviors and predict a sizable BCD that gives rise to a potentially detectable Hall voltage. Our findings open up opportunities to integrate electrical and magnetic modulations of the nonlinear Hall effect within a single material, with potential applications in multi-state information encoding and readout in antiferromagnetic spintronics.

title: Organizational Learning in Materials Discovery Campaigns: Which Databases, Calculations, and Agent Teams Pay Off
abstract: More databases can make a materials campaign worse. Through an organizational lens, we trace each source's contribution. One band-gap campaign ranks seven anion families from archived measured gaps, one vote per source. In the first half of its budget, all seven pooled rank worse (rank agreement 0.737; 1 = measured order) than the best pool of three (0.851). As a stability check, choosing the pool on half the runs and testing on the rest kept the gap. Splitting Materials Project afterwards points to its transition-metal oxides and fluorides. Two databases from one pipeline add nothing over one, but pooling gives their shared ordering two votes. New calculations repay their cost early only when two or three campaigns reuse them. Flat language-model agent teams trailed a random-pick baseline (mean 0.876, sd 0.096, 20 searches). An adaptive Al-Mg-Si team, mostly interatomic potentials, was scored on unseen HSE06 calculations. In its first quarter of compute it found 49% of the ten lowest-formation-energy compounds, against at most 40% for fixed teams and 73% for MACE-MP-0 alone. Merging members whose orderings agreed carried most of its gain. This suggests pooling a few sources that fit the measurements, counting each pipeline once and charging for computation.

title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
abstract: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision. A single request can launch calculations for an entire collection of molecules, without requiring a separate LLM decision for every compound. This design limits the information the model must process as screening collections grow, while keeping the underlying results available for inspection and further analysis. The integrated tools support molecule generation, prediction of binding and molecular properties, and searches for compounds available for purchase. In a retrospective comparison with an expert-led campaign, the agent proposed chemically distinct candidates with competitive docking scores and higher calculated drug-likeness under explicitly imposed selection criteria. In a 22-task benchmark against plain tool calls and Codex, the agent achieved the highest observed mean model-judged score, with lower median cumulative token use and peak context. Fármaco provides a foundation for flexible, scalable drug discovery workflows that connect scientific reasoning with an enduring, traceable record of computational work.

title: Possibility of Potts Spin-Ice in Rare Earth Twisted-Kagome Layers: an Example of DyAgGe
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin-ice compounds, predominantly based on the pyrochlore or spinel structure, have been attracting considerable interest in the last two decades. A two-dimensional (2D) analogue is the spin-ice consisting of kagome planes. So far, only Ising spin ice has been discovered in any material, and only one 2D material, the kagome compound HoAgGe, has been identified as a spin ice. In this Letter, we show that another rare-earth twisted Kagome magnetic compound, DyAgGe, is in fact a Potts spin ice (or color ice), where at each site not two but four spin directions are allowed. We argue that an 8-state spin ice may also exist in this class of systems. We present a first-principles calculation of magnetic interactions in DyAgGe, and confirm the 4-state Potts structure of this material by matching our model predictions with the available experimental data.

title: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization
abstract: Therapeutic antibody development is often framed as comprising two discrete stages: initial discovery of novel binders followed by iterative optimization to refine these hits into therapeutic-grade molecules. Models and methods often reflect these stages, with generative structure models applied to discovery and probabilistic black-box optimization methods applied to refinement. Here we propose to unify these stages by smoothly transitioning a generative discovery model into iterative optimization, allowing the handoff between the structure-based prior and supervision from wet lab data to be guided by the posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate. We show that this yields improvements in optimization efficiency in the low-N regime, as well as improved diversity amongst the optimized molecules.

title: Isothermal-Isobaric Molecular Dynamics with a Foundation Interatomic Potential in LAMMPS across NVIDIA and Intel GPUs
abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer one model for many chemistries, but their deep, globally coupled architectures do not fit the spatial decomposition that scales classical and short-ranged MLIPs. We present pair_style uma, a LAMMPS pair style that evaluates the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) through LibTorch on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs from a single source tree. It reimplements FairChem's edge-sharded graph parallelism in C++ over exported TorchScript modules, with one MPI rank per device, NCCL or oneCCL collectives, and the whole energy and force path in double precision. The strain-gradient virial is carried through the exported modules and the cross-device reductions, so that fix npt runs on both vendors' hardware. We measure NPT capacity and cost on one 4xA100-40GB node, one 8xH200 node, and one 12-tile Intel node, and on up to 32 Intel nodes. Without activation checkpointing, one node holds NaCl cells of about 8,000 atoms (A100, 0.21 ns/day), 22,000 atoms (Intel, 0.10 ns/day), and 47,000 atoms (H200, 0.16 ns/day). Graph parallelism raises the capacity of a single device by 8.0x on H200 and 4.6x on A100. Across nodes, capacity grows to about 779,000 atoms on 32 Intel nodes, with a slower speed at 0.007 ns/day. On H200 and A100, a FLOP count of FairChem's graph-parallel predictor gives lower bounds of 31% and 51% of FP64 peak. From one omat checkpoint and with no refit, nine 100 ps NPT heating ramps (NaCl, equiatomic Pt-Ru, and equiatomic (HfNbTaTiZr)N, on all three node types) ran to completion.
